title: Ring links: pass_link tries only the straight chord, so fig8 lifts where an edge route would stay down

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## Problem

After PR #3818 (#3747), fig8 with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside still has 18 named lifts. A second review of #3818 found that these lifts are mostly a gap in the planner, not a real need:
- 9 lifts give the reason "would cross a cut";
- 9 lifts give the reason "would leave the area";
- no lift is for a fixture.

`pass_link` tries only the straight chord. It does not try `edge_route`, which walks the edge of the area. The ring links of `ring_links::link` use `edge_route`, but the pass links do not.

## Expected

- `pass_link` also tries `edge_route`, with the same proof (`linkable`, `chord_clears` on the cutter-centre area) before it lifts.
- A lift stays only when no straight chord and no edge route is clear. It keeps its named reason.
- The pin `lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason` also checks a maximum count of lifts. Lower the maximum to the count that remains after the fix.

## Notes

- P1 by the maintainer's rule: each outcome issue of the #3741 family is P1.
- The maintainer's words on #3741: the tool "should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool".
- Related: #3822, #3743, #3750.

labels.name: bug

body:
## Problem

PR #3818 (#3747) applies the ring link law to each `around_part` area that has a chosen pass start. `around_part` is true for each Clearing operation with Outside containment and a stock. This includes a 2D Pocket with Outside containment, as `crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs` uses it (`pocket_op` sets `Containment::Outside`).

The PR body says "2D Pocket Inside and Outside do not change (#3752)". But the joins and pass links of such a pocket now use the ring law. The review of #3818 found that the change is safe: every link is proved, or else it lifts with a named reason. But no pin covers it.

A second point from the same review: for a ring area, the ring law overrides `Link::Clearance` and `Link::KeepDown`. A failed link lifts to `hop_z` (retract), not to `clearance_z`. A user who selected Clearance can expect the clearance height.

## Fix

Choose one of these, and record the choice in `docs/decisions/`:
1. Narrow the gate to the 2D Offset operation, so that 2D Pocket waits for #3752.
2. Keep the scope, and add pins for a 2D Pocket with Outside containment: no overcut, no crossing, and each lift named.

Also decide if a failed link honours the user's `Link::Clearance` choice. Pin the result.

## Notes

- P1 by the maintainer's rule: each outcome issue of the #3741 family is P1.
- Related: #3752 (2D Pocket on the shared ring set), #3743.

title: Apply max_stay_down to the plan join and the edge route

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## What happens

The ring-link law reads `max_stay_down` on the pass link at `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs:118`. It does not read it on the planner join and the edge route at `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_order.rs:264-269` and `ring_links.rs:158`.

Thus the edge route can stay down longer than the value the user set.

## Why it matters

The limit is a user promise. The tool misses a lift that the parameter asks for. This is not a gouge: the review of #3818 proved each chord stays in the cutter-centre area.

The straight join has the same gap before this change.

## Fix

Apply `max_stay_down` to each chord of the planner join and the edge route, in the same way as the pass link. Add a pin with a small `max_stay_down` and assert the lift.

## Scope

Found in the review of #3818 at head `968fa46d7`.

title: Column stock: simulate copies the whole cut history on each call, so a program cut one move at a time is quadratic

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_sim::cut::simulate` (the column engine behind `Stock::simulate`) copies the stock's whole cut history at the start of each call:

```rust
let mut history = dex.history.as_deref().cloned();
```

The history holds every cut so far. It grows with each call. A caller that cuts a program in small steps (one move for each call) thus copies a longer history at each step. The total time is quadratic in the number of moves.

Expected: the time of a program cut one move for each call is near the time of the same program cut in one call.

### Evidence

We run `camcraft-sim` from a fork as the stock engine of a batch verifier. The verifier reads the stock before each cutting move, thus it cuts one move for each call.

- A 3-axis job on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, 137,940 moves: one call takes 2 s. One move for each call ran for more than 1800 s, and we stopped it.
- With the history grown in place (below), one move for each call takes 6 s. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a column stock: `Stock::block(Backend::Column, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 20.0, 10.0, 0.1)`.
2. Make 4000 short feed moves across the block.
3. Cut them in one `simulate` call. Then cut them on a second, new block with one `simulate` call for each move.
4. Compare the times. The second cut is much slower, and the gap grows with the number of moves.

### Proposed fix

Take the history out of the stock, grow it in place with `Arc::make_mut` (this copies it only when another stock shares it), and put it back. On a refusal, truncate the cuts to their old count and put the history back, so the stock stays as it was (`add_ops` only appends cuts). We have this change and a pinning test on our fork. We will open a PR from a branch `issue/3819-history-in-place` if you accept the claim.

Not in scope: `carried::clip_columns_under` uses the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (slow with a workaround: cut in one call), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor).

Done means: a pinning test in `camcraft-sim` cuts 4000 moves one call at a time on a column stock. Each column top is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, and the time stays inside a linear budget.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at with fixtures (avoid route): the Arc entry does not start in air outside the stock box

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during #3746.

## What happens

#3746 gives the Arc entry of a start-side pass (2D Offset, "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside round a part) a plunge in air outside the stock box and a G17 arc onto the first ring. The change is in `pocket_started_on` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`, `air_entry.rs`).

The avoid route (`pocket_avoid_started_on`, used when the op has fixtures or clamps to avoid) builds its own `Motion` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, near the `with_cleared_links` call). That `Motion` has no air room. Thus with fixtures, the Arc entry keeps the old behaviour: "the arc's lead room is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead". The dive is named, so it is not silent.

## Why it was not done in #3746

The air outside the stock box is proved free only of the part. On the avoid route, a fixture or a clamp can stand outside the stock box. The air room must subtract the keep-outs of the avoid spec (grown by the tool radius) before a lead can use it.

## Done means

- The avoid route passes an `AirRoom` whose legal area is the cutter-centre area joined with the air outside the stock box, less each keep-out grown by the tool radius.
- A pin on the dog-bone part with a clamp outside the stock box: the plunge stands outside the box by the tool radius plus the approach distance, and the lead does not touch the clamp.

title: Name the edge and the vertex in the 'a vertex sits off its edges' refusal

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## What happens

The import of `twisted_flank_off.step` is refused at `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs:158-169`. The refusal names solid `#117`, the 0.343 mm gap and the 1e-3 mm limit. It does not name the edge or the vertex.

This came with the solidcore bump of PR #3802 (head `c2399c040`). The old kernel named the face.

## Why it matters

The user cannot see which part of the model is wrong. The information is in the candidate: `body.worst_edge` holds the kernel edge and the vertex point.

`check_source_topology` at `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs:94-101` already writes the same value as "Input-record edge index N, vertex (x, y, z) mm".

## Fix

Map `body.worst_edge` to the input-record edge, and to the face when the record has it, in the refusal at `record.rs:158-169`. Use the same form as lines 94-101.

Then `crates/app/tests/import_step_twisted_flank.rs` can pin the face or the edge again.

## Scope

The file is still refused. The toolpath output is not wrong. The defect is a missing detail in the refusal text.

body:
## Problem

On Windows, agents commit some files with CRLF line endings, while `main` uses LF. In PR #3790, 10 files came in with CRLF. A 5-line change in `generate.rs` showed as about 4500 changed lines, and the churn caused two of three merge conflicts. PR #3737 had the same problem with two files.

## Fix

- Add a `.gitattributes` at the repository root with `* text=auto eol=lf`. Add explicit `binary` rules for PNG, STEP, STL and other binary fixtures, so that Git never changes them.
- Do not renormalize the whole tree in the same PR. If files on `main` have CRLF now, list them and normalize them in one separate commit.
- Check that the snapshot PNGs, `tests/golden/*`, `.cl` and `.cnc` fixtures are not changed by the rule.

## Notes

- Found by the review of PR #3790.
- `.gitattributes` is not a process file. The PR needs a normal review.

title: Adding a catalog tool above the mounted machine's max rpm says nothing until verify holds the post (EM-0300-2FL 15000 rpm on a 10000 rpm 770MX)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

On a mounted Tormach 770MX (ML) (`spindle_max` 10000 rpm), `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` and `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0400-2FL" }` copy the catalog's 15000 and 12000 rpm into the document as they are. Nothing says they are above the machine: the `add_tool` reply carries only the holder note, `add_operation` and `generate` add no note, and the first word of it is the machine check at verify / post, which holds the program:

```
machine Tormach 770MX (ML): 2 limit problem(s): 2D Adaptive1: tool EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the machine's 10000; 2D Contour1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs 12000 rpm, above the machine's 10000
```

The block itself is right (the Prime Directive holds: no over-limit S word is posted). The defect is that it comes last, after the work is generated, and that the other paths that set a speed already hold it to the machine and say so:

- `apply_cutting_data` / `suggest_cutting_data` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs`, `compute`): "45094 rpm held to the machine's 10000".
- the Feeds tab spindle row (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs`, `hold_to_machine`): "spindle speed N rpm held to the machine's maximum M".

Only adding a catalog tool (MCP `add_tool`, `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` -> `AddTool::with_holder`) takes the catalog rpm with no reading of the mounted machine. The verify problem also does not say what to do about it (edit the tool's speed, or `apply_cutting_data`).

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate. Script `b.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script b.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("set_stock", {box: {dx: 37.4, dy: 37.4, dz: 5.27}});
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0400-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-0400-2FL", source: "simple"});
cam.generate();                       // generates, no rpm note
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.verify())); // gate ok:false, the problem above
```

## Expected

When a tool is added (MCP `add_tool`, and the UI's add from the catalog) while a machine with a `spindle_max` (or `spindle_min`) is mounted and the tool's rpm is outside it, the reply / status says so at once, e.g. `"warning": "EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the Tormach 770MX (ML)'s 10000 - the post will be held; set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data"`. The machine check at verify keeps blocking as now, and its problem line names the same fix. The tool's rpm is not changed silently by the add (a library speed stays what the user stated; the warning tells them).

## Where

- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` (the reply has `note` for the holder only).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs` `AddTool` (where a note like the holder note can be built from the mounted machine).
- `crates/post/src/machine/check.rs` and `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`: the "runs N rpm, above the machine's M" problem text, which could name the fix.
- For comparison: `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` (`compute`, the clamp with a note) and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs` (`hold_to_machine`).

Related: #3457 (the lathe sibling: catalog TN-1600-0R8's 3000 rpm over the Tormach 15L's 2500, a first post held).

Priority P7 (a late refusal that could say more and an owed warning; the block is correct and the workaround is plain: edit the speed or apply cutting data). Effort medium: a note in one command's reply and the UI add path, plus the problem wording, with a test; posted G-code, the machine check and the gate do not change (if the fix instead clamps the rpm at add, it changes posted S words and is effort:high by the safety floor).

Done means: with the Tormach 770MX (ML) mounted, `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` returns a warning naming 15000 rpm and the machine's 10000, the UI's catalog add shows the same text, a tool within the range gets no warning, and verify still blocks the post with a problem line that names the fix; pinned by a test in `crates/app/tests/`.

title: 2D Adaptive on the stock: a stock margin narrower than the tool is refused as "pocket is narrower than the tool", with no band, width or fix named

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

A 2D Adaptive on the stock (source `stock`, no boundary picks) around a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate, stock from **fit stock** (2 mm per side, top Z 3.27), with a 3 mm end mill (catalog `EM-0300-2FL`), on the Tormach 770MX (ML), refuses at generate with:

```
2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool
```

The refusal is right (the area to clear is the 2 mm band of stock around the part, and a 3 mm cutter has no legal position in it), but the message does not say that. There is no pocket in this job, so "pocket" points the user at the wrong thing. It does not say which area is narrow, how wide it is, by how much the tool misses, or what to change. The in-app assistant read it as a missing boundary selection or a too-small helix radius (0.6 mm), and neither is the cause.

Readings (box stock, `dz` 5.27, side margin m per side, same tool and op):

| margin per side | result |
|---|---|
| fit stock (2 mm, Z -2..3.27) | refused: "pocket is narrower than the tool" |
| 1 mm | refused, same text |
| 2 mm | refused, same text |
| 3 mm (= tool D) | generates (Offset rings fallback, notes) |
| 4 mm, 6 mm | generates; the #1655 band note and corner note appear |

So the band check that #1655 added (`machining2d::unreached_note` through `operation::keep_law::narrow_noted`) names a narrow band only when some other part of the area produced a path. When the whole area is one band narrower than the tool, the generator refuses first, with the bare sentence, and the band note never runs.

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate STEP (any plate of that size works). Script `a.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script a.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("fit_stock", {});            // 29.4 x 29.4, Z -2..3.27: 2 mm per side
cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.generate();
```

Output: `generate: 2D Adaptive1 - could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool`. Replace `fit_stock` by `set_stock {box: {dx: 31.4, dy: 31.4, dz: 5.27}}` (3 mm per side) and it generates.

## Expected

A refusal that says what is narrow and what to do, e.g. "2D Adaptive1: the stock around the part is a band 2.000 mm wide, narrower than the 3.000 mm tool (plus 0.000 mm stock to leave): no cutter position fits. Widen the stock to at least 3.000 mm per side, use a tool under 2.000 mm, or cut the outside with a 2D Contour." The same refusal stays a refusal (no path is emitted); only its words change. Where the area is a real pocket (a part source, a closed boundary), the text names the pocket and its narrowest width the same way.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs` `pocket_started_on` (the site this job hits: `non_sliver_center(region, off)` empty -> `GenError::Invalid("pocket is narrower than the tool")`), and the same bare sentence in `adaptive_avoid.rs`, `pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, `rest_prior.rs`, `corner_relief_spur.rs`, `adaptive/rest/mod.rs`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` `narrow_noted` / `machining2d::unreached_note` (#1655): already measures the band; it could word the refusal when the whole stock-around-part area is one band.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs` `name_outside_entry_refusal` already adds advice to this sentence, but only for Outside containment (#2232), not for the stock source.

Related: #1655 and #1554 (the band note on a generated path), #3631 (warn at edit time when the tool cannot fit a pocket; this issue is the generate-time refusal text, not the edit-time warning).

Priority P3 ("a misleading message" with a workaround: widen the stock or pick a smaller tool). Effort medium: the refusal stays a refusal and no toolpath, gouge check or posted G-code changes (so the safety floor does not apply); the work is wording in the 2D pocket family plus reuse of the existing band measure, with a test.

Done means: on the reproduction above (stock-source 2D Adaptive, 2 mm stock margin, 3 mm tool) generate is still refused, and the refusal names the stock band around the part, its width (2.000 mm) against the tool (3.000 mm), and at least one fix (wider stock or smaller tool), without the word "pocket"; a pinning test in `crates/app/tests/` asserts that text, and the existing "narrower than the tool" asserts still pass.

title: 2D Offset one ring set: full-width cuts where the rings of two lobes merge (fig8 waist), and the narrow note does not name them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found while fixing #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside). Related: #3743.

## What happens

The one ring set of #3744 is the offsets of the part. At a concave place of the part, the offsets of two lobes merge. At the merge, the corner of each ring moves by more than one stepover from the corner of the next ring. Thus some cuts there take the full tool width.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step` (the `offset_pass_start` heavy fixture: EM-0800-4FL, stock margin 5 mm, Outside containment):

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are the first ring along the part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to the stock box) | 0 |

- The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures the distance to the nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near the merge are inside that distance, so the "narrow" note does not come.
- This is a load issue, not a gouge. The gouge and crossing checks are clean on this pass.

## Expected

- The rings at a merge do not take the full tool width. One option: clean-up rings or a smaller local step between two ring corners that are more than one stepover apart (Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991, covers the merge of offset curves).
- A cut that still takes the full width is named on the path, by the same law that the flanks meter uses.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): #3744 moved its reading from 0 to the bound "at most 520 points, all in the waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads the full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:medium

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Aur package; should rebuild the Linux build that comes before it and not rebuild it again from scratch.. Waste of time and action credits." He set the priority P2.

## Problem

In `release.yml`, the AUR package step compiles CamCraft again from the source. The `linux` job of the same run has already built the same release binaries from the same tag. The second build costs time and billed GitHub Actions minutes (AGENTS.md: the minutes are budgeted).

## Expected

- The AUR package uses the Linux release binaries that the `linux` job of the same run made. Use an artifact (`actions/upload-artifact` in the `linux` job, `actions/download-artifact` in the AUR step), or the release asset of the same tag.
- The AUR package does not run `cargo build` again.
- The PKGBUILD that we publish stays correct for AUR users. If the AUR rules need a from-source PKGBUILD, publish it unchanged, and only the CI check of the package uses the prebuilt binaries. Record which way was chosen, and why, in `docs/decisions/`.
- The packaged binary is byte-identical to the binary in the Linux release asset. A check compares the checksums.

## Notes

- This changes a file in `.github/workflows/`. Use the `runners` skill. Add no trigger. The maintainer ordered this change.
- Measure the minutes of a tag run before and after, and put the numbers in the PR body.
- Test the change with a `workflow_dispatch` dry run, not with a new tag.

body:
The site tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`) run only in the `site` job of `release.yml`, after the tag. Thus guide drift is found only when the deploy fails. This happened at v0.25.0 (#3271) and again at v0.26.0 (#3763).

No gate tier runs `site/tests`. The quick, batch and release tiers of `cargo xtask gate` do not include them, and `cut.yml` stage gate does not run them.

Proposal (the recommended option):
- Add a step to the release tier of `cargo xtask gate` that runs the site tests with the pinned zola 0.23.6, so that `cut.yml` stage gate fails before the tag.
- Optional: add the same step to the batch tier, so that `post-merge.yml` finds the drift on each push to `main`.

A change to `.github/workflows/` needs the maintainer's approval (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted"). A change in `xtask/` is a process change.

Done means: a PR that adds an operation, a post hook or a manifest property without its site page makes a gate red before the cut.

Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750). Step 5 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "Each ring goes around the part in the plane of the cut and stays at depth. The tool does not lift between the parts of one ring."

## What happens

Circular has its own ring code: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs:233-340` (`rho = rc - stepover * k` at `:289`, the Inside order at `:288`, the rim helix at `:300`). It walks each ring as its own ladder (`run_level_walks` for each ring, `:340`). Each call makes a new `WalkState` with `first: true` (`levels.rs:328-329`). Thus each ring enters again from the clearance height, and each entry goes down into material. The rings are not linked at depth.

## Fix approach

1. Circular gets its rings from `ring_set` with the circle input. The rings stay exact G2/G3 circles at the same radii.
2. One walk for each level over all rings. The link from ring k to ring k+1 is a stepover link at depth by `ring_links` (a radial line or a tangent arc in the cut plane).
3. One entry for each level by `ring_entry`. The rim helix stays as the entry where the tool must enter material.
4. A lift needs a named reason.

## Pins

- `circular_rings_link_at_depth`: a circular pocket with 4 rings has one entry and 0 lifts on each level.
- `circular_rings_unchanged`: the ring radii and the arc count of each ring are the same as on the head before this change.
- Equivalence: the verifier verdicts and the gouge checks of `crates/motion/tests/circular_arcs.rs`, `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` do not change, except the lift and entry counts.

Effort `max`: a new link law for Circular, under the safety floor. Priority P1: a needless lift and an entry into material at each ring.

Done means: Circular rings come from `ring_set`, each level has one entry, and the pins are green.

Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750) and on #3744. Step 2 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason."

## What happens

2D Pocket uses the same start-side planner as 2D Offset, with the dead-end ramps on (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:314-318`, `ring_plan_ramped(..., true)`). Thus a Pocket with Pass starts at Inside or Outside has the defects of #3741: other rings for each start side, a lift at each piece, and the #3577 dead-end ramps.

Pocket Waterline and OffsetRings use a second planner (`waterscan.rs:62-216`, through `pocket_plan.rs:20-36`). Its rings are chained only where a chord is clear (`waterscan.rs:217`). Each other pass break lifts by the `Retract` pass link of `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`, `ladder_links.rs:163`), with no proof and no reason.

## Fix approach

1. 2D Pocket gets its rings from `ring_set` with `RingRef::Boundary` (the walls and the islands, Held 1991). Waterline, OffsetRings, Inside and Outside all use it. Pass starts at changes only the order of k and the start point.
2. The links between rings use `ring_links`. A lift has a named reason.
3. The entry uses `ring_entry`. A closed pocket has no air path, so the first entry is a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column, or the user's helix or ramp. A pocket that is open to the stock edge enters in air.
4. Remove the Pocket call of `ring_plan_ramped` and of `plan_passes` for the ring strategies.

## Pins

- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: on a square pocket with a round island, Inside, Outside and Waterline give the same multiset of rings (1 um, after a start-point and direction normalisation).
- `pocket_rings_do_not_lift`: the same pocket has 0 lifts on one level. Each lift on the fig8 pocket has a named reason.
- `pocket_has_no_dead_end_ramp`: no ramp along a pass on a start-side Pocket.
- Equivalence: the ring radii, the verifier verdicts and the gouge checks of `crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs` and `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs` do not change, except the lift counts and the entries that this issue fixes.

Effort `max`: a planner change under the safety floor. Priority P1: needless lifts and ramps into material in the posted program.

Done means: 2D Pocket rings come only from `ring_set`, the pins are green, and each lift has a reason on the status line.

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Make the camcraft-cli able to interact witht he ui. By adding the flag --ui, so it instead sends it commands directly to the UI and changes gets reflected in the UI. This allows for alot better interaction and end2end testing, for dealing with UI improvements and for endusers also doing setups. The CLI improvements should come with a --skill <folder,claude,copiplot> install creating a AI skill for working with the CLI tool."

The maintainer set the priority P2.

## Part 1: `camcraft-cli --ui`

- With `--ui`, the CLI does not run the commands in its own headless world. It sends them to a running CamCraft UI.
- The UI runs each command through the same undoable command history as the GUI ("Everything Is a Command"). The change shows in the UI at once, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
- The CLI prints the result of each command and returns a non-zero exit code on an error, as in headless mode.
- When no UI is running, the CLI gives a clear error. It does not fall back to headless mode silently.
- Uses: end-to-end tests of UI changes, agent-driven checks of the UI, and set-up of a project by a user from a script.

Questions to decide (record each in `docs/decisions/`):
1. The transport: a local socket or a named pipe. Find the UI with a discovery file in the user's data folder. Bind only to the local machine.
2. Security: accept only local connections from the same user. Use a token in the discovery file. Never listen on a network port.
3. The protocol: reuse the MCP tool surface (`crates/app/src/mcp/`) so that the CLI, MCP and the GUI call the same commands. Do not make a second command set.
4. Several UI windows: select one by project path or process id.
5. Windows, Linux and macOS from the same source ("Stays buildable everywhere").

## Part 2: `camcraft-cli --skill <target> install`

- `<target>` is one of `folder`, `claude` or `copilot`.
- `folder`: write the skill files into a given folder.
- `claude`: install the skill where Claude Code reads skills, for the user or for the project.
- `copilot`: install it where GitHub Copilot reads custom instructions.
- The skill text comes from one source in the repository, and it lists the CLI verbs, the `--ui` mode and examples. Relate it to #1947 (single-source AI agent skills) and to the existing `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- A test checks that the installed skill names each CLI verb that exists (a drift test).

## Pins

- A UI test starts the app through the test harness, sends one command with `--ui`, and checks that the UI state changed and that undo restores it.
- A CLI test with no running UI checks the clear error and the exit code.
- A test for each `--skill` target writes into a temporary folder and checks the files.

## Notes

- This is new design (an IPC transport and a protocol), thus effort:max.
- Slices are permitted: part 1 first, then part 2.

body:
Part of #3743. Builds on #3744 (the one ring set of 2D Offset). This is step 1 of the migration of #3743. Each later step uses the modules of this issue.

## The maintainer's words

#3743: "so we are not having 18 different ways of doing ring planning."

#3741: "The only thing that differs and inside and outsided strategy is actually where the tool starts.. inside the bounding box, or outsided the bounding box."

## What to do

Move the ring code of 2D Offset (after #3744) into three shared modules in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`. The output of 2D Offset must not change.

1. `ring_set`: the one ring planner.
   - Input: the cutter-centre area (`center`), a reference edge (`RingRef::Part` = the selected contour, the 2D Offset; `RingRef::Boundary` = all walls of the area, the pocket), the first offset, the stepover, the chord tolerance, and an optional circle (a disc area gives exact circle rings).
   - Output: rings with their index k, closed or open, clipped by the cutter-centre area.
   - The start side (`PassStart`) gives only the order of k and the start point. Auto selects Inside or Outside by the #3744 rule.
2. `ring_links`: the one linking rule. Stay at depth. Link ring to ring in the cut plane. The link proof is `link_proof` + `through_cut` (`ladder_links.rs:230-261`). A lift needs a reason, tallied with `LinkTally::lift` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:142-175`).
3. `ring_entry`: the one entry rule, in this order:
   1. An entry in air outside the stock box, by the approach distance (#3745), then a G17 arc lead in the cut plane (Arc radius, Arc sweep) onto the first ring (#3746).
   2. A proved pre-drilled hole (`predrilled.rs`).
   3. A cleared column that an earlier cut opened.
   4. A helix or a ramp into material, only where the tool must enter material (a closed pocket with no air path).
   5. Else a refusal with a named reason. Never a silent plunge.

If #3746, #3747 or #3748 merge before this issue, move their code into these modules too. If this issue merges first, they put their code into these modules.

## Decision record

Write `docs/decisions/3743-shared-ring-planner.md` on this branch. It records the shared design of the #3743 research (result 2 on #3743). It also records the pass link default for ring passes:
- Recommended: a new seed `Links::RINGS` (`pass: KeepDown`, else as `PLANAR`) for the ring ops. A ring op of an old project file that stores the `PLANAR` default loads as `RINGS`, because `Retract` at each pass break is the defect of #3741 and #3423. A user who sets Retract by hand gets Retract, and the status line says so.
- Dropped: keep `Retract` for old files (the old files keep the needless lifts). Dropped: ignore the user's pass link (it removes a user parameter).

## Pins (equivalence)

- `offset2d_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner`: 2D Offset with Auto, Inside and Outside on the dog-bone part of #3741 and on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` gives the same CL moves as the head before this change (a golden `.cl` in `tests/golden/`, recorded on that head).
- The verifier verdicts and the gouge and collision checks of `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs` and `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels.rs` do not change.
- Unit tests of `ring_set`: a disc gives circle rings at `rc - k * stepover`; a square with an island gives the same rings for `RingRef::Boundary` as `waterline_passes` (`waterscan.rs:62`) within 1 um.

Effort `max`: a new shared planner contract, under the safety floor. Priority P2: a consolidation with identical output.

Done means: the three modules exist, 2D Offset uses only them, the pins are green, and the decision file is on the branch.

Part of #3741. Builds on #3746 (the air entry) and #3747 (the in-plane links).

## The maintainer's words

"you would never helix on a outside cut.. as you dont need to "lead in" like that.. so an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut, starting outside the stock boundary with a given value."

From the #3741 comment: "An Outside cut never uses a helix entry, and it does not use a ramp entry." Pin: "an Outside pass has no helix move and no ramp move into material, and that each entry starts outside the stock boundary."

## What happens

A start-side pass can still enter by a helix or a ramp at four places:

1. The first entry of a level: `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`) with the user's Helix or Ramp; `descent.rs:131-136` (a helix stands down to a ramp).
2. The #3577 dead-end ramp: `level_ramp_entry.rs:100-127` (`dead_end_ramp`), marks at `level_order.rs:143-145`, plan check at `level_rings.rs:108`, call at `ladder_links.rs:188-191`. Decision: `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md`.
3. The #2265 solid restart between passes: `ladder_links.rs:200-211`.
4. The centre-cutting law stand-ins: `descent.rs:137-148`.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part; see the #3741 research comment): Outside on `main` has 366 ramp moves (13 dead-end ramps). On `47aa341ff^1` the same 13 re-entries were plunges or helices.

## Fix approach

1. After #3746 and #3747 a start-side pass has one entry for each level (the air entry) and no re-entry into uncut stock. The dead ends of #3567 do not exist with the contour-parallel rings of #3744.
2. Remove `dead_end_ramp`, its marks (`ramp_starts`) and its plan check. Update `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md` with a "superseded by #3741" line.
3. On a start-side pass, a restart that would need a helix or a ramp lifts and uses the air entry, or the op is refused with a named reason. It never helixes or ramps into stock.
4. Rewrite the pins of `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs` that assert a ramp ran. The late-entry pin counts every entry into stock again (no ramp exemption).

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_pass_has_no_helix_or_ramp`: Inside and Outside on the dog-bone part and on `testdata/models/fig8.step` have no helix move and no ramp move below the material top.
- `start_side_entries_start_outside_the_box`: each entry of a start-side pass starts outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` (existing, `pass_start_engagement.rs:181`) stays green with no ramp exemption.

Effort `high`: removal of one entry law and its pins, under the safety floor.

Done means: the pins are green, `dead_end_ramp` is gone, and the #3567 decision file names #3741.

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set). Covers Inside and Outside (and Auto through #3744).

## The maintainer's words

"Simulation show that the path approach breaks down, instead of "going around the" object in the plane, it "lifts over" it picking up the contour ont he other side and starts ramping down back and forth to the desired depth again.. Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

About Inside: "And it also does a shit ton of uncessary lifts.."

The rule from the #3741 comments: each ring goes around the part in the plane and stays at depth. Where a ring is split, the link stays in the plane when the path is clear. A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason.

## What happens

1. The 2D Offset uses `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`; `crates/app/src/operation/types/links.rs:65-67`). Its pass link is `Link::Retract`. `pass_link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs:154-225`) then lifts at every pass break, with no proof and no reason (`:161-163`, `:182`).
2. With `Link::KeepDown`, `link_proof` (`:243-261`) and, for a start side, `through_cut` (`:230-237`, `cleared_links` at `pocket.rs:346`) refuse a link between two Outside pieces that end on the part wall: the chord crosses the part.
3. The planner joins two pieces only when `linkable` (`level_order.rs:110-151`). Each other piece is a new pass, thus a lift.
4. After each lift the re-entry is the #3577 dead-end ramp (`ladder_links.rs:188-191`) or the #2265 solid restart (`:200-211`). This is the "ramping down back and forth".

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level; see the #3741 research comment):

| Pass starts at | lifts (Retract) | re-entries | lifts (KeepDown) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 13 | 14 |
| Inside | 8 | 7 | 7 |
| Auto | 7 | 6 | 7 |

The Outside counts are the same on `e313aa663` (#3353). #3577 changed only the kind of re-entry.

## Fix approach

1. With the one ring set of #3744, link ring k to the next ring at depth by a stepover link in the cut plane. The link runs through the band that the next ring cuts.
2. Make the in-plane link the rule for a start-side pass, whatever the pass link of `Links::PLANAR` is. A lift needs a reason.
3. Where the stock edge splits a ring, link the pieces in the plane through cut material or air when the chord clears the part and the fixtures.
4. Lift only when each in-plane link would hit the part or a fixture. Tally the reason with `st.tally.lift(why, ...)` and show it on the status line.
5. Check #3423 (P7, lifts between pieces) and close it as covered when this merges.

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_rings_do_not_lift`: on a part with no split ring (a disc in a larger stock box), Inside and Outside have no lift and no re-entry on one level.
- `dogbone_start_side_lifts`: on the dog-bone part, count the lifts and re-entries of one level for Inside and for Outside. Each lift has a named reason in the notes. Expected: 0 lifts when each link clears the part.
- `lift_reason_is_named`: a fixture across the in-plane link gives one lift, and the status line names the fixture.

Effort `max`: a new linking law with a collision proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the three pins are green, and the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` with Inside and Outside has only lifts with a named reason.

"The arc atm, is showing as a "straight" plunge down.. which is fine for transporting to the plane, but it should happen outside the stock box. - and also we see no movement of a an arc to wal into the wall of the stockbox - so no viable approach is getting generated using the Arc approach. The Arc Sweep and Arc Radius inpputs does nothing to affect the approach"

About Inside: "picking "inside" makes perfect rings, but the cutter planges straight down into the material.. instead of starting outside the stock box"

## What happens

Inside and Outside share one entry path: `ladder_links.rs:55-92` (`descend`) -> `descent.rs:120-149` (`plan`) -> `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`). One fix covers the two.

1. The entry is placed at the first point of the first pass (`descent.rs:217`). For Outside that point is on the stock edge. For Inside it is at the part wall, in solid stock.
2. The `Arc` entry is a vertical-plane arc onto the first cut (`entry.rs:37-41`, `descent.rs:262-277`). Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area (`descent.rs:271`). For Outside that area ends at the stock box, so the air outside the box is never legal. `entry_arc.rs:146-152` returns "the arc's lead room is blocked".
3. `descent_dive.rs:169-187` (`substituted_dive`) then posts "axial dive on the floor instead". Its fix text (helix radius, start hole) does not apply to a start side.
4. The horizontal (G17) arc entry (`arc_xy`, `descent_xy.rs:205-220`) is skipped when the arm is `Arc` (`:218-219`), and it proves only inside the legal area.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2; see the #3741 research comment):

- Outside, Arc entry: the first dive has its tool centre 0.50 mm INSIDE the stock box. Arc radius 4 -> 10 and Arc sweep 90 -> 45 do not change the path.
- Inside, Plunge entry: 8 plunges; the first one is 8.41 mm inside the box, in solid stock.
- Same on `e313aa663` (#3353): this is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

A new entry law for a start-side pass (Inside and Outside, and Auto through #3744):

1. Rapid to a point P outside the stock box. The distance from P to the box is at least the tool radius plus the approach distance (#3745).
2. Feed down in air at P to the cut Z.
3. Feed in the cut plane: an optional straight lead, then a G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent onto the first ring. Arc radius and Arc sweep come from `Approach::arc_radius` / `arc_sweep`.
4. Prove the lead path against the stock box grown by the approach distance and the tool radius, not against the cutter-centre area. It must not touch the part or a fixture. Where no lead fits, refuse with a named reason. Do not post a silent plunge.
5. Outside: the first ring is at the stock edge, so the lead runs in air and enters the stock wall on the arc.
6. Inside: the first ring is at the part wall, and stock can enclose it. Recommended option (the maintainer's words): the entry still starts in air outside the box, and the in-plane lead feeds through the stock to the first ring. This feed is a slot at the full tool width, so it uses the plunge feed and the status line names it. Dropped: a helix in material for Inside (the maintainer asks for an air entry). Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
7. Check the Lead in / Lead out page. The maintainer saw Helix, Ramp and Plunge disabled for Outside. That page code was not found on `main` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs:25-44, 89-102` show all four kinds). Make the page offer only Arc and a straight approach for Inside and Outside.

## Pins (red first, from the maintainer's comment)

- `outside_entry_plunges_in_air`: the plunge XY is outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`: the first cutting move after the plunge is a G17 arc at the cut Z.
- `arc_radius_changes_the_lead`: a change of Arc radius changes that arc's radius in the output; a change of Arc sweep changes its sweep.
- `inside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`: no entry of an Inside pass is a straight plunge into material (the maintainer's pin).
- `start_side_entries_have_no_helix_or_ramp`: no Inside or Outside entry is a helix or a ramp.

Effort `max`: a new entry geometry with a new legal-area proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the five pins are green on the dog-bone part and on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step`.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at: one contour-parallel ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside; the choice changes only the start point and the ring order

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #3741. The other sub-issues of #3741 build on this one.

## The maintainer's rule

His words (chat, 2026-11-23): "The only thing that differs and inside and outsided strategy is actually where the tool starts.. inside the bounding box, or outsided the bounding box. Why there is different cut strategies between outside, inside and auto (which is insane) is strange.."

Also: "contour-parallel offset rings from the outside in toward the selected contour" (the #3741 body, Expected).

## What happens

"Pass starts at" selects one of three different ring planners. Each gives a different set of rings.

- Dispatch: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:101-120` (`ring_plan_ramped`).
- Auto: `pocket_plan.rs:20-36` -> `waterscan.rs:62` (`waterline_passes`). It offsets the whole cutter-centre area from both edges. In a long narrow band the loops collapse to thin back-and-forth loops. The maintainer sees "zigzag or raster-like moves in the long side areas".
- Outside: `level_rings.rs:188-203`. The rings are offsets of the outer edge only (the stock box). The part cuts each ring into open pieces that end on the part wall.
- Inside: `level_rings.rs:169-187`. The rings are offsets of the part, grown out. They are parallel to the selected contour.
- Other start-side switches: `pocket.rs:308-347` (`cleared_links`, `ramp_starts`), `pocket_avoid.rs:147, 209-210`, `pocket_hsm_start.rs:42-63`, `pocket_hsm.rs:61-62, 92-100`, `level_order.rs:143-145`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:982, 1102` (the stock band goes to the plan only when the start is not Auto).

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part in an 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level; see the #3741 research comment):

| Pass starts at | floor runs | runs that end on the part wall |
|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 14 |
| Inside | 8 | 0 |
| Auto | 7 | 1 |

This started with #3353 (`e313aa663`). It is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

1. Make one ring set for the three choices: the contour-parallel rings, at the distances `off + k * stepover` from the selected contour (the part), cut by the cutter-centre area of the stock box. This is the ring set of the Inside branch today.
2. The rings that the stock edge cuts are open pieces. Keep them in the same set.
3. Inside walks the rings from the part out (k up). Outside walks them from the stock edge in (k down).
4. Auto selects one of the two start points. It does not select a different planner. Recommended rule: Auto = Outside when the stock box is larger than the cutter-centre area on all sides (open air around the stock), else Inside. Record the rule in `docs/decisions/`.
5. Remove the Auto-set fallback of `level_rings.rs:113-118` for the start sides, or make it give the same ring set. A leftover area gets clean-up rings of the same set, not a different planner.
6. Delete the start-side switches that only exist because the ring sets differ (`cleared_links`, the dead-end marks). The linking and entry sub-issues of #3741 replace them.

Check the other users of `level_pieces` and `plan_passes` (2D Pocket, `pocket_avoid`, the 3-D pocket levels). #3743 reviews all 2D ring planners. This issue is the 2D Offset slice of that review.

## Pins (red first)

- `inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: on the dog-bone part, Inside and Outside give the same multiset of rings (each ring as a closed or open polyline, compared within 1 um after a start-point and direction normalisation). Only the ring order and the start point differ.
- `auto_is_inside_or_outside`: Auto gives exactly the path of Inside or of Outside on the same part.
- `outside_rings_follow_the_part`: on the dog-bone part, no Outside floor run ends on the part wall, except at a ring that the stock edge cuts.
- `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`: on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` (through the existing test loaders), Inside and Outside give no `Warning::Crossing`. (The maintainer's Inside run gave 414 Crossing warnings on a private model. The synthetic part gives 0.)

Effort `max`: a new ring planner contract for three choices, under the safety floor (it changes posted G-code).

Done means: the four pins are green; Auto, Inside and Outside of 2D Offset call one ring planner; the decision file records the Auto rule.

title: 2D ring planning: review all ring planner strategies of the 2D operations and reduce them to one shared planner

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## Why

The maintainer asked for this research in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Add a heavy P2; needs-research ticket, where all ring planner strategies (2D ops) are getting propeprly re-reviewed, so we are not having 18 different ways of doing ring planning."

#3741 shows the problem. Inside, Outside and Auto of 2D Offset use different code paths. They give different entries, different links and different lifts. The maintainer's rule for #3741 is: one ring planner, and the choice changes only the start point.

## Scope

Each 2D operation that makes contour-parallel rings or offset rings, for example:
- 2D Offset (Inside, Outside, Auto);
- 2D Pocket and the 2D ring and chain kinds;
- 2D Adaptive, where it makes rings;
- Face, Slot, Circular, 2D Contour with several passes;
- Engrave and Trace, where they offset;
- each other 2D operation that the research finds.

## Questions

1. List each ring planner, ring linker, entry chooser and lift rule in the 2D operations. Give the path, the line range and the operations that use it.
2. For each one, give what it does that the others do not, and whether that difference is needed.
3. Which defects come from the differences? Link the open issues (for example #3741 and its sub-issues).
4. Propose one shared design: a ring planner, one linking rule (stay at depth, link in the plane, lift only when an in-plane link hits the part or a fixture, and name the reason), and one entry rule (an entry in air outside the stock where possible, an arc lead-in in the cut plane, and a helix or ramp only where the tool must enter material). Each operation then gives only its own parameters.
5. Give the migration order, one operation at a time. Give the equivalence pins that each step must keep: the same rings, verdicts and gouge checks, except for the defects that it fixes.

## Output

- Answers in comments on this issue.
- One sub-issue for each migration step. Each one is effort:high or effort:max (safety floor: toolpath motion), with its pins.
- A decision record of the shared design in `docs/decisions/` on the first sub-issue's branch.
- Close this issue when each part is covered by a sub-issue.

## Notes

- Clean-Room Protocol: use published CAM literature and our own design notes only.
- #3741 goes first. Its fix must not wait for this research, but it must be compatible with the shared design.

body:
## Report

The maintainer reported this bug in chat on 2026-11-23. Build: v0.26.0 `f729592f0` (the release branch `release/v0.26.0`).

His words: "When choosing "outside" on the page "Passes" the planner creates a path that is only "linear" with alot of uncessary lifts and transports.. instead of just do a circular motion from the outside into the mode. Not keeping the dool down, following the countour of the selection.. Instead it does a b unch of ramped cuts that would break the crap out of the cutter following the approach of the entry tab states and then offset cut following the selected contour.."

## Setup

- Operation: 2D Offset. Source: Selection. Tool: Ø8 end mill (EM-0800-4FL).
- Passes: Stepover 2.0 mm. Pass starts at: Outside. Stock to leave: 0.0 mm. Arc turns at corners: on. Arc radius = tool radius: on.
- Heights: Clearance = top of stock +10.0 mm. Top = top of stock. Bottom = selection bottom +1.5 mm. Stepdown 40.0 mm (one level).
- Status line: `3566 moves (7 plunge(s) @ 300, 1 level(s), 210 arc(s)), 0 warning(s)`. Turn blends: 169 of 1221 pass corners rounded, 457 of 1221 kept sharp.

## Seen

- The path from the stock edge toward the contour is many short linear segments.
- There are many lifts and transports between the segments.
- Many segments start with a ramped entry, as the Lead in / Lead out page sets.
- After these segments, the operation does the offset passes along the selected contour.

## Expected

- With "Outside", the tool enters one time outside the stock.
- It then stays down and cuts contour-parallel offset rings from the outside in toward the selected contour, with a stepover link from ring to ring.
- There are no lifts and no repeated ramped entries between the rings.

## Why P1

Repeated ramped entries into material and many short engagements can break the cutter. The posted program is wrong for the selected strategy.

## Notes

- PR #3577 merged on 2026-11-23 (`47aa341ff`). It changed the entry of a dead-end later Outside pass to a ramp along the pass. Check it first as a possible cause.
- PR #3620 merged on 2026-11-23. It changed the verifier slices. Check it as a second possible cause.
- This issue was found after the v0.26.0 cut line (2026-11-23T19:22Z). By the cut rules it is not on the cut list. The maintainer decides.

title: A review finding keeps the PR ready: no draft round trip for needs-rework

body:
The maintainer asked for this change on 2026-11-23: "Do your changes as a docs changes, push it and merge it and announce it one go.. On my call."

What the data shows (30 PRs, 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-23, 36 times a ready PR went back to draft):
- 27 of 36 followed a `needs-rework` label. 17 came from our own reviews and 10 from the author's reviewer.
- 3 followed a `conflicts` label. 6 had no label cause.
- The median time from ready to draft is 1.6 hours.
- #3283 and #3284 flipped three times each. #3061 returned four times for one class of defect.

Each round trip costs one more read and one more trial.

The change:
1. A `needs-rework` finding does not turn a ready PR back into a draft. The author pushes the fix to the same PR. A push moves the head, so the earlier review and `merge-ready` do not count for the new head.
2. An orange `conflicts` verdict still makes one of our own PRs a draft.
3. The first `needs-rework` comment names the class of each finding and asks for one rule that closes the class.

Done means: AGENTS.md, the `review-prs` skill and the `resolve-conflicts` skill say this, a decision file records the maintainer's order, and PROCESS_VERSION is bumped and announced on #681.

Split from #3186. PR for #3186 does the asset selection, the catalog check and `plan::may_run_ignored` for directory suites. This issue holds the `quick.rs` part.

Today `quick.rs` runs the whole binary of a directory suite in these cases:

- `map_modules` (`xtask/src/quick.rs` about line 181) joins the Gate maps of all the module files of a suite. A src change selects the whole binary.
- A change outside the `#[test]` fns of one submodule sets `p.whole` (`quick.rs` about lines 103-133).

Change `quick.rs`:

1. Match each Gate map for each source file (`suites::Source`), not for the joined text.
2. When only some submodules match, or when one submodule changes outside its test fns, pass a libtest module filter: `--test <suite> <submod>::`.
3. Run the whole binary only when `main.rs` or a shared module changes.

This needs a new pick kind (a module filter for each binary) in `Picks`, in `describe` and in `steps`.

Done means: `xtask` unit tests show that a change in one submodule of a directory suite plans `--test <suite> <submod>::`, and that a change in `main.rs` plans the whole binary.

A second item from the #3186 work: `may_run_ignored` keeps the old rule for a flat suite. A `mod x;` line makes a flat suite heavy. About 175 flat suites with `mod common;` and no `#[ignore]` in their files get a heavy step at the cut (measured with `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`). A walk of `suites::sources` for flat suites too removes these steps. Do this only with a review of the cut plan.

Part of #919.

## What happens

In a mm program, the Haas post rounds each feed to a whole number of mm/min. For a G84 tapping cycle the feed is pitch x spindle speed. The control cuts the pitch F / S. A rounded F gives a wrong pitch.

2. Refuse a pitch and speed pair whose feed the format cannot write exactly.

body:
**What happens**

`ff()` in `assets/posts/haas.cps` rounds an mm feed to a whole number of mm/min. For example, 12.4 mm/min posts as `F12.`. An inch feed keeps two decimals. #3681 (PR #3689) added the decimal point and did not change the precision. A positive feed that rounds to zero keeps its fraction since #3681. A feed of 1 mm/min or more is still rounded.

**Why it matters**

The error is under 0.5 mm/min. At a low feed it can be a large part of the value. Examples are a slow finish pass, a G84 tap feed that must equal pitch x rpm, and a probe touch feed. A tap feed that is not exactly pitch x rpm can damage the thread or the tap.

**What should happen**

Decide the mm feed precision, for example one or three decimals, as the length words use. Then regenerate the Haas goldens. Check the tap feed first: it must not lose the pitch x rpm value.

**Done means**

- A test posts a fractional mm feed (for example 12.4 mm/min) and a tap feed, and checks the F word.
- A decision file records the precision and its source.

Found during #3681 (PR #3689).

title: Haas post writes F words with no decimal point: at the default of Setting 77 the control reads F600 as 0.6 mm/min

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens**

haas.cps writes an F word with no decimal point. In mm, `ff()` writes every feed as a whole number: it returns `String(Math.round(v))` (assets/posts/haas.cps, function `ff`). In inch, `trimNum()` removes the point from a whole value, so 50.8 mm/min posts as `F2`.

The Haas goldens show it. For example, crates/app/tests/golden/nc/haas/arc_planes.nc, line 15:

```
G18 G3 X15. Y0. Z0. I-5. K0. F600
```

**Why it is wrong**

On a Haas mill, Setting 77 (Scale Integer F) sets how the control reads an F word that has no decimal point. Source: Haas Mill Operator's Manual 96-8000 rev V (January 2009), Settings, "77 - Scale Integer F". In mm at the DEFAULT value (.001), F1 is F.001, so F600 is 0.6 mm/min. At INTEGER, F600 is 600 mm/min. The manual says: "It is recommended that programmers always use a decimal point."

The post cannot know Setting 77 on the machine. With a decimal point, the control reads the same feed at all values of Setting 77.

#1836 fixed the same problem for the length words: `pt()` adds the point. `ff()` does not use `pt()`.

**What should happen**

Every F word that haas.cps writes has a decimal point, for example `F600.`, `F23.62` and `F2.`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Post a mill operation in mm with the Haas post, or open crates/app/tests/golden/nc/haas/arc_planes.nc.
2. Look at the F words. They are `F600`, not `F600.`.

Version: main 8c6b77f94 (v0.25.0-519). Linux.

**Done means**

- `ff()` always writes a decimal point, in mm and in inch.
- The Haas goldens show `F600.` and the other feeds with a point.
- A test fails when haas.cps writes an F word with no decimal point.

Not checked: the other posts.

Found while: we posted a 3-axis test part through haas.cps (CamCraft 0.25.0, machine haas-vf2ss.mch) for one of our Haas VF-2SS YT mills. All feeds had no decimal point.

We have a fix with two tests on our side. We can send it as a pull request.

title: 3D Finish links: check if a hop with a retract height below the end of the run feeds the tool down into the part

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in the review read of PR #3625 (#3362). **This is a hypothesis from a read of the code. No test or run shows it yet. The first step is a test.** The priority is `P1` because the possible result is a gouge that passes; correct the priority when the test gives the answer.

## What the read found

`emit_runs` in `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/march.rs` (about lines 347-390 on `main` at `7c637d705`), the plain hop between two runs (about lines 381-383): the travel height is `trav = hop.max(z0)`, where `hop` is the retract height and `z0` is the Z of the start of the next run. The Z of the end of the current run (`cur.z`) is not in the formula. The hop is not checked against the model.

If the run that ends is higher than the start of the next run, and the retract height is below `cur.z`, the tool moves down at the current XY to `trav`, and then makes a rapid across at that height. At the current XY the tool is on the surface. A move down from there goes into the part.

## Where it can occur

- On `main` today: a cavity with the Contour or Flat pattern (the outer pass is high, the inner pass is low), when the retract height of the operation is below the high pass.
- With PR #3625 and `Pass starts at: Inside`: a convex part (a dome), because the inner pass is high and the next pass is lower.
- With a retract height above the top of the part (the usual setup) the fault cannot occur: `hop` is then above `cur.z`.

## Not known

1. Whether a rule refuses a retract height below the top of the part when the operation is made or edited.
2. Whether the verifier gives a blocking finding for the move down and for the rapid across.

## Wanted

1. A test, first: a cavity fixture on `main` with Contour, a retract height between the two passes, and the verifier. Read the moves of the hop, and the findings.
2. If the tool goes into the part: `trav` must not be below `cur.z` (for example `hop.max(z0).max(cur.z)`), and the rapid across must be checked like the other links (`diagonal_ok` / `straight_ok`) or go to the clearance height. Pin it for a cavity and for a dome.
3. If a rule already refuses that retract height, or the verifier blocks the post: say so here, pin that fact, and set the priority to `P3` or close the issue with the pin.

The decision file of PR #3625 says that each link "is certified by the existing laws". Correct that sentence for the plain hop when the answer is known.

title: The verifier slices at every cut Z: an interpolated ramp turns 3 planes into 1,700 and minutes into hours

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
The verifier slices the part at every distinct cut Z. A path with an interpolated ramp has about 1,700 cut planes instead of the 3 cut levels, and the band-reach and tangency laws then take minutes. The same path takes 89.6 s as a whole suite on main.

## Evidence

From PR #3577's head (one Waterline Outside generation, debug, temporary counters, reverted):

- The generator is fast: `ring_plan_ramped` 110 ms; each level walk 1.5 to 1.8 ms; 186 `dead_end_ramp`/`push_zig` calls are all in microseconds.
- The path is 8,850 moves and 8,553 feed moves, with 1,697 distinct feed-move Z values (the cut levels are 3: z = 12, 2, 1.5).
- The time is in the verify laws:
  - `section::tangency` 28.3 s;
  - `section::solid` 0.82 s;
  - `band_reach` plane sections and grid 1.4 s, with 5,596,906 boundary samples at a 2.75 mm cell;
  - `band_reach` verdict loop: moves 0 to 6000 in 55 ms (all skipped by the `h0 >= stock_top_z` guard), then more than 148 s without finishing for the remaining 2,850 moves; single moves take 2.8 s and 28 s, about 150k `sample_tests` per move.

The unmodified single test was killed at 120 s: 100 percent CPU, 0.1 s system time, 471 MB RSS. It is CPU-bound.

## Cause

The new dead-end entry posts a zig-zag ramp, one feed move per thinned vertex per lap (`crates/motion/src/links.rs`, `push_zig`). `Rest::new` (`crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs:89-100`) records one cut per feed chord, keyed on `m.to.z`. The path therefore has about 1,700 distinct cut planes. `band_reach_counted` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:47`, the plane loop at 102-110 and the verdict loop near 205-240) slices the part at every distinct cut Z, so the work is `O(feed_moves x samples)`, and samples grow with the plane count: quadratic in the number of ramp Z steps. `section::tangency` (`crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:89-146`) pays the same per-distinct-Z cost through `rest.islands_at`.

The new planner code is ruled out: `level_order.rs`, `level_rings.rs` (`order`, `unswept`, `too_short_at`), `level_ramp_entry.rs`, `descent.rs::ramp_fallback`, `links.rs::plan_zig_capped/push_zig` and the `arc_cross` retries are all sub-millisecond to about 100 ms.

## Recommended fix

In `band_reach_counted`, build the sampled plane set from the cut LEVELS (feed moves with `|from.z - to.z| < z_tol`) plus the deepest cut, instead of every `rest.cut()` record, and pass that set to the same `islands_at` and `boundary_samples` code. For this path that is 3 to 4 planes and restores the pre-PR cost; the same plane set also removes the 28 s in `section::tangency`.

This slightly reduces wall-sample coverage for ramps between levels. The heavy lanes on a sloped or stepped fixture must show that the verdicts do not change before it merges. A lower-risk variant is to quantize the plane key and cap the sample count.

## Why #3595 did not cover it

#3595 (`9a7de3781`) made the sample lookup exact and fast. It did not reduce the number of planes, so the per-plane cost stays.

## Related

- #3577: the ramp entry that exposes this; blocked until this is fixed.
- #3588: the verifier speed work, closed by #3595.
- #3587: the slow pin as a test-speed item.

title: Stock preview: a ray that uses all its march steps is discarded, so the cut stock shows holes that change with the view

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A user reported this in chat on 2026-11-22.

## What happens

In the simulation, the traced stock picture shows holes in the stock. Through a hole, the user sees the viewport grid behind the stock. The holes are on the faced floor, near the tool path. When the user orbits the camera, the holes change shape. Thus the cause is in the picture, not in the stock data.

The user saw this in a local build. The exact version is not known.

## Expected

The picture shows the stock as solid where the stock has material. A pixel that the march cannot resolve does not show the background as if the stock were cut through.

## Cause (from a read of `origin/main` f35202134, not built)

- `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` gives each ray `MAX_STEPS = 64` steps. Each step is `phi * RELAX` (0.9).
- Near a large flat face, at a low view angle, `phi` is small. The steps become small, and the ray uses all 64 steps before a hit. The ray returns status 2 (unreadable).
- `crates/ui/src/trace/composite.wgsl` (lines 47-50) discards each pixel that is not a resolved hit. The traced picture replaces the stock slot, so nothing is drawn behind the pixel. The user sees the background.
- The comment there says that a budget bail is "never painted as material". That rule is correct. But a hole also gives a wrong picture: the stock looks cut through.

## Not affected

The Deviate verdict, the post gate and the STL export do not read the traced picture. The G-code is not affected.

## Possible fixes

1. Paint a budget bail at the last march point, with a tint that shows that it is approximate. Do not discard it.
2. Increase the step budget, or set a minimum step near a surface (for example a fraction of the cell).
3. Keep the CPU twin (`camcraft_sim::stock_sim::preview::march`) in parity. The parity test is `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.

## Related

- #3336: stock simulation performance.
- The `machined.rs` mesh is not shown when the GPU eye traces. A separate change can show the mesh when the transport is down.

Done means: a grazing view of a faced stock floor shows no background pixels inside the stock outline. A test pins this on the CPU twin, and the GPU parity test stays green.

title: Project save writes over a `.camproj` that changed on disk, with no warning: the other changes are lost

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happened**

A save replaces a newer project file on disk with no warning, and the other changes are lost.

When the `.camproj` file on disk changed after CamCraft opened or saved it, the next save to that file writes over it. The save does not check the file first, and no message shows. The work that the other window, program or person saved is gone.

Nothing records the file's state when a project is opened or saved:

- The window: `State::save_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4722`) calls `project::save` directly. `State::open_project_path` (`state.rs:4669`) reads the file and keeps only its path.
- The script call `cam.save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41`) and the MCP tool `save_project` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:152`) do the same. Without a path, `save_project` "saves over the file last opened or saved".
- The only file-stamp checks in the UI are for linked models and theme files (`crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs:94`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files.rs:130`).

This can occur when:

- the same project is open in two CamCraft windows;
- a `git pull` or a branch switch changes the file while CamCraft is open;
- a colleague saves the same file in a shared folder;
- a sync client (OneDrive, Dropbox) replaces the file with a version from another computer.

**Expected**

Before a save replaces the project's own file, CamCraft checks that the file did not change since it was opened or last saved. If it changed:

- the window asks before it writes (overwrite, save as another file, or cancel);
- a script or an agent gets a refusal that names the file, and can give an explicit overwrite option.

SolidCraft has the same behaviour: its `file.save` refuses such a file unless `overwrite` is set.

**Steps to reproduce**

I found this by code inspection. I did not run these steps on a machine.

1. Open `job.camproj` in two CamCraft windows, A and B.
2. In B, add an operation and save.
3. In A, make a different change and save.
4. Open `job.camproj` again: the operation from B is gone. No window showed a message.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at `60b19abe8` (2026-11-22). The same code is in v0.25.0. Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- Remember a disk stamp of the project file (path, size, modification time) at open and after each save. It reads no file content, so a large project costs the same as a small one.
- Before a save to that file, take the stamp again. If it is different:
  - the window shows a prompt: **Save As**, **Cancel**, **Overwrite**. Nothing is written before the answer;
  - `cam.save` and `save_project` refuse by name. `save_project` gets an optional `overwrite` argument, and `cam.save` gets an options object `{ overwrite }`.
- A save to another path, a new document, and a file that was deleted are not checked.
- An agent attached to the window uses the window's stamp, so its save is checked too, and the window does not ask about the agent's own save.
- `project::save` and the file format do not change.

**Done means:** when the project's own file on disk changed after the open or the last save, a save to it is held in the window and refused for scripts and MCP. `overwrite: true` (or Overwrite in the window) replaces the file. Tests show the refusal, the overwrite option, and that a save directly after our own save is not refused.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.
