title: Verifier: band_reach takes minutes when a toolpath has many cut planes (a ramp entry)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the work on #3567 (PR #3577, the ramp entry at a dead end).

## What happens
The verifier `camcraft_sim::verify::verify_bodies` takes minutes for a 2D toolpath that goes down by ramps. Measured in debug on the test `pocket_pass_start::fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`:

| Tree | Time |
|---|---|
| `main` (4c0a157e1) | 89.6 s, pass |
| PR #3577 at e7ae538a3 | more than 1500 s (stopped) |
| the same with the ramp thinned to the arc-fit tolerance | more than 9 minutes (stopped) |

The planning and the emit of the path take 0.21 s (8850 moves, 33 passes). The time is in the verifier:
- crossings: 0.0 s;
- tangency: 34.7 s for 2232 moves that are not planar;
- solid: 1 s;
- `reach::band_reach` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:72-80`): not complete after 3 minutes.

## Cause
Each ramp move ends at its own Z. `band_reach` slices the model at each different cut Z (`rest.islands_at`), adds the boundary samples of each slice to one sample set, and tests each move against the whole set. The cost is about moves x planes x samples. A path with helices, as on `main`, has few planes. The tangency check slices one time for each different Z also (about 15 ms each in debug).

The same cost can come from any path with many different Z values: a ramp entry that a user selects today, a helix with a small pitch, a 3D path. A user waits minutes with no progress and no message. The Prime Directive asks for a clean result, not a hang.

## Wanted
- `band_reach` keeps the island samples for each plane and tests a move only against the planes that it reaches (or an index by Z), so that the cost does not grow with moves x planes.
- The cache key of `islands_at` and the tangency slices are checked for the same pattern.
- A test with a ramp of many small moves pins a time or a count bound (a count of slice calls is better than wall time).
- The findings of the verifier do not change: pin them on the existing cases (this is a collision and gouge check, under the safety floor).

## Why P2
PR #3577 (the fix of #3567) cannot merge before this: with it, a 2D Offset or 2D Pocket with Pass starts at Outside takes minutes to verify. Measure the release build also and correct the priority if it is seconds there.

title: A script cannot open a project in the CamCraft window without taking the focus

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A script starts `camcraft-ui some.camproj` from a background process. The window takes the foreground. The script cannot prevent this.

## What happens (CamCraft 0.25.0, Windows 11)
- The launcher sets STARTUPINFO `wShowWindow` to `SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE` (7) or `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` (4). This has no effect.
- The window is visible and not minimized at about 40 ms after launch.
- The window is the foreground window from that time.

I polled with EnumWindows, IsWindowVisible, GetWindowRect and GetForegroundWindow.

## Cause (found in the code)
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_window.rs` (`init_gpu`) creates the window with default attributes. In winit 0.30.13 a visible, active window is shown with `ShowWindow(SW_SHOW)` (`window_state.rs`, `apply_diff`).
- The same function then calls `window.focus_window()`. On Windows this sends a synthetic Alt key press to get past the foreground lock, so the lock timeout does not matter.
- Nothing in the program reads the launcher's show state.

## Proposal
Two new start options in the `cli_options` table:
- `--no-activate`: create the window inactive and do not call `focus_window()`. The window shows, and the focused window keeps the focus.
- `--minimized`: the same, and the window starts minimized. It covers no other window.

The default does not change. A separate step could read STARTUPINFO on Windows. That is a larger change, so it is not proposed here.

A patch is ready on a branch. It has unit tests for the parser and the window attributes. I also checked both options with the project on the command line, from a process started by Task Scheduler (not from a terminal). The window was never the foreground window, and it did not take the focus when the project finished loading. `--minimized` gave a minimized window. Not tested: macOS, Linux.

Is this the wanted shape?

title: Drilling: check if a hole tilted some degrees from the tool axis is recognized as a Z hole and drilled along Z

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by reading, in the second read of PR #3502. It is not a fault of that PR: the code is on `main`. **Nothing was run. This is a hypothesis.** The first step is a test that proves or disproves it.

## The hypothesis
The hole recognizers `recognize` and `recognize_cross` (`crates/motion/src/drilling/recognize.rs:87,97`) classify a hole from its wall facets with `WALL_NZ 0.7` and a circle fit with `FIT_TOL 0.02` (`recognize.rs:39,44`), in the setup frame.

A hole whose axis is tilted 2 degrees from the tool axis has a section that differs from a true circle by about 0.0006 r. That is far below the fit tolerance. Such a hole can pass as a Z hole. The drilling operation then drills along Z, and the drill cuts into the wall of the real hole. This is a gouge that passes with no message.

## Why P1
If the hypothesis is true, the posted program cuts in the wrong place and nothing blocks the post (the table: "a gouge or collision that passes").

## Wanted
1. A test with a part that has one hole tilted 2 degrees and one tilted 5 degrees from the tool axis (made from code, no model file). Assert what detection gives for each: a Z hole, a skipped hole with a name, or a cross hole.
2. If a tilted hole is taken as a Z hole: a tolerance on the angle of the axis (small, for example the angle at which the drill moves the wall by more than the tolerance of the operation over the hole depth), and a named skip for a hole outside it. Record the tolerance as a decision. Consider a parameter with a default (CAM choices are user parameters).
3. If the test shows that detection already refuses or skips the tilted hole: keep the test as a pin and close this issue with the commit.

body:
Found during the bounded search of #3319 (2026-11-22).

## What happens

The part-solid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:214-237`) judges each rapid against the part solid. When the tool body or its edge column meets the part, it pushes `Warning::RapidInStock { at: i }`.

That warning prints this text (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:467-468`):

`rapid move N travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)`

The text is wrong for this case:
- The rapid can be vertical (a lift out of a pass, or a drop to a pass start).
- The rapid can be at or above the clearance plane at one end.
- The tool meets the part, not the uncut stock.

The user then reads it as a lateral G0 under the clearance plane. This is what happened in #3319.

## How to see it

Headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`, on `origin/main` 835556814 and on v0.25.0 (7e2a8119c):
1. `import_model` `testdata/models/fig8.step`; `add_tool` `EM-0800-4FL`; `fit_stock` box, sides `[5,5,5,5,0,2]`.
2. `edit_tool` `{"flute_len": 10}`.
3. `add_operation` "2D Offset" on the bottom face (Z 0), containment Outside. Clearance = Top of stock +10, Top = Top of stock +0, Bottom = Selection +1.5, Stepdown 10, Entry Helix r 1.6, `retract_z` null.
4. `generate`, then `verify`.

Result: `shank_hit` on moves 1406-1658 and 2194-2446 (the outer ring of levels 2 and 3), and `rapid_in_stock` on moves 1659, 2193 and 2447. Moves 1659 and 2447 are the vertical lifts to Z 32 at (-0.202, -33.998). Move 2193 is the vertical drop to Z 4 at the same point. Each lateral G0 of the posted program (a long-flute copy of the same path) is at Z 32.

The post is blocked, so the output is safe. Only the message is wrong.

## Done means

- A rapid that the part-solid law convicts gets a message that says the tool meets the part on a rapid, and that names the move.
- `rapids.rs` keeps its text for a rapid through the stock.
- A pin test in `crates/sim/tests/` shows the two texts on the two cases.
- The MCP `kind` string and the UI severity stay correct for the new text.

title: Project save writes the `.camproj` file in place: a failed write destroys the old project

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happened**

`project::save` writes the new project text directly into the target `.camproj` file (`crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:296-304` on `main` f14097855):

```rust
if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(path, &text) {
```

`std::fs::write` truncates the file first and then writes the new bytes. If the write stops before the end, the old project is gone and the new project is incomplete. This can occur when:

- the disk or the USB stick becomes full;
- the connection to a network share stops;
- the app or the computer stops during the write.

A cloud-sync client (OneDrive, Dropbox) or a backup tool can also read the file while it is half written, and copy the incomplete file to other computers.

All save routes use this function:

- the window: `State::save_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4716`);
- the MCP tool `save_project` and the script call `cam.save`: both go through `api::v_save` to `crate::project::save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:49`).

I found this while I examined how CamCraft projects behave in shared and synced folders.

**Expected**

A failed save keeps the old `.camproj` file as it was. Other programs never see a half-written project file.

CamCraft already does this for machine files and for the fixture library. `machine::store::write_atomic` (`crates/app/src/machine/store.rs:104`) writes a temporary file in the same folder, flushes it, and renames it over the target. On a failure, it removes the temporary file, and the target stays as it was. `fixture_library/store.rs` has its own copy of the same steps (line 107).

**Steps to reproduce**

I found this by code inspection. I did not make a damaged file on a machine.

1. Open a project and save it to a `.camproj` file.
2. Read `project::save` in `crates/app/src/project/wire.rs`: the save opens the existing file with truncation before it writes the new text.
3. Any failure after step 2 leaves a short or empty file in the place of the old project.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at f14097855 (2026-11-22). The same code is in v0.24.0 and v0.25.0. Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- `project::save` calls `machine::store::write_atomic`. Preferences, recent files, view settings and machine files already use this helper. No new module and no new copy.
- Two refusals of today stay:
  - a save into a folder that does not exist (the helper creates missing folders, so `project::save` checks first);
  - a save over a read-only `.camproj` file. On Linux and macOS, a rename replaces a read-only file, so `project::save` checks first.
- The file format and the saved text do not change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.
- The browser build does not change. It gives the text to a download (`save_text`), not to a file path.
- On Windows, a rename can fail when another program holds the target file open. The save then reports the error, and the old file stays.

**Done means:** `project::save` replaces the target only through a rename of a complete, flushed temporary file in the same folder. A test shows that a failed save keeps the old `.camproj` byte for byte. A test shows that a good save leaves no temporary file. Tests show that a save into a missing folder and a save over a read-only file are refused, and that the old file stays. The `project_roundtrip` tests still pass.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

body:
Follow-up of #3466 (item 3 of that issue). The fix for #3466 is in the shipped posts only.

3. Each shipped post that writes tilted moves declares the flag. Each such post has a posting test of the real order (see `crates/post/tests/upright_after_tilt.rs`).
4. A Mach4 pin in that test file (the AC trunnion fixture of `mach4_trunnion.rs` must move to a shared helper first).

Found by the second read of PR #3471 (comment 7081078749 on that PR). It is a reading of the code and of the usual control behaviour. It is NOT confirmed by a run, and no control ran it. The first step of the work is to confirm or to disprove it. If it is confirmed, this is wrong posted G-code and the priority goes to `P1`.

PR #3471 stops a G2/G3 block whose written end point equals its written start point (#3442). One more case stays: only the radial axis word changes between the start and the end of an arc, and the written start is within half an output step of the line through the centre. Then the written start and the written end have the same angle about the centre. A control that reads an equal angle as a full turn can cut a spiral of nearly one full turn.

By reading, this needs a radius below about 0.05 mm with mm output (3 decimals), or about 0.3 mm with inch output (4 decimals).

## Necessary work
1. A recorded input with such an arc for the mm case and the inch case. Post it with `fanuc.cps` and `linuxcnc.cps`. Show the blocks.
2. Find from public documentation of the two controls how each reads an arc whose start and end have the same angle and different radii.
3. If the block is unsafe: extend the guard of `crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs` (for example, check the turn direction and the sweep from the WRITTEN words, and post a linear move when the written sweep is not the sweep of the record). Add the case to the table test over all posts.

Refs #3442

## What is wanted

A Part (part-off) operation has no parameter for the position of the kerf. Since #3452, the whole kerf of the blade is always on the waste side of the parting plane (the end face of the finished part).

title: Fanuc and Doosan posts: an upright operation after a tilted operation states no rotary angles, so it can run with the axes still tilted

labels.name: P1

labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

body:
Found by a read of `origin/main` (f14097855) on 2026-11-22, after a note in the second read of PR #3421. It is NOT confirmed by a run: the first step of the work is a test that posts such a program.

## What the code does
A program has two operations in one setup: first a five-axis operation that leans the tool (5-Axis Contour, Flow, Swarf), then a 3-axis operation with the tool upright.

1. The tilted section ends with the tool still tilted. Its exit rapids keep the pose (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`, near line 210).
2. `dump()` in `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` keeps the state `tilted` for one operation only (lines 430 and 520-541). The first upright move of the next operation gets no angles.
3. `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: `endPreamble` (786-838) resets `tcpmOn` and `lastA/B/C` in the script only. `startPreamble` (742) writes `G49` only. No block writes `A0` or `B0`. `retractHome` is `G28 Z0` with no rotary axis.
4. `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `endPreamble` (873-905) resets `lastA/B/C` only. `startPreamble` writes `G49` only.

Result, by reading: the posted program has no rotary word between the last tilted move and the first cut of the upright operation. The machine stays at the last tilted angles, and the 3-axis operation cuts with the tool or the table tilted. That is wrong posted G-code (a gouge or a collision), and no check stops it:

- `first_traverse_posed` judges only the first operation of the post order (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3325`).
- No check compares the pose at the end of one operation with the start of the next.

## Posts that are safe, by the same read
- `tormach.cps` writes `G53 G0 Z` and `G0 A0` at the first upright move of a section (718-775).
- `mach4.cps` writes `G00 A<zero> C<zero>` when the stored lean is different (about 575-625).
- The posts that refuse a tilted move cannot post the first operation.

## Necessary work
1. A test that posts a tilted operation followed by an upright operation with `fanuc.cps` on `tilthead.mch` and with `doosan-dnm.cps`. It shows the blocks between the two sections. If the program states the angles, close this issue with that evidence.
2. If it does not: each section that follows a tilted section states the rotary position before its first approach, at a safe height (the pattern of PR #3421 for the opening of a tilted section, and of `tormach.cps`). The same for a tool change between the two, and for the same tool in the two operations.
3. A check in the app: an upright operation after a tilted one posts only when the return to upright is stated, else a refusal with a diagnostic.
4. The same test for each post that supports a rotary axis.

Context pack: `.claude/tmp/context/stale-tilt-between-sections.md` (local). PR #3421 changes the same code (`post/mod.rs` `dump`, `stamp.rs`): stack on it.

Refs #3300

body:
From the merge-order analysis of 2026-11-22. AGENTS.md, "Heavy lanes at review" (#2568): the author runs `cargo xtask gate heavy` on the final head of each PR whose diff reaches a heavy lane. One run of the motion and app lanes takes 60 to 70 minutes, and only one heavy build can run at a time on a machine. For a wave of 9 PRs that reach the lanes, this is about 12 hours.

## Proposal (the maintainer decides; this changes AGENTS.md)
A wave of PRs that the planner puts in one group can use ONE heavy run on the trial tree of the wave: the current `main` with each PR of the wave merged. The run covers each PR, because the tree contains each diff. The result is recorded on each PR of the wave (the tree hash, the lanes, the counts). If the run is red, the red step is attributed to a PR, that PR leaves the wave, and the run starts again for the rest.

Rules that stay:
- "Not run" is never a pass.
- A PR that merges alone keeps the rule of today.
- The release tier at the cut stays the final check.

## Necessary work
1. A decision entry in `docs/decisions/` with the maintainer's answer.
2. The text of AGENTS.md ("Heavy lanes at review") and of the `gate`, `merge-ready` and `review-prs` skills.
3. `cargo xtask gate heavy` accepts a trial tree and prints the list of the PR heads that it covers.

The PR has `Process change: yes`.

"findings": [],

Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582), brief q03 (turned pin, 70 mm long), CamCraft **v0.25.0** Linux x86_64 release, Tormach 15L Slant-PRO, post Tormach PathPilot Lathe. The G-code below was read by hand against the model.

## What happens

The part spans WCS Z 0 (front) to Z -70 (back face, with a 1 x 45° head chamfer at Z -70..-69); the bar runs on to Z -84. Op7_Part_Off: kind `part`, tool GT-0300 (3.0 mm wide grooving blade, orientation 2), `bottom_z` = bottom of model. Posted (q03-turn-shaft.nc lines 1813-1858):

```
(T0404 Parting_3mm - GROOVING BLADE ORIENTATION 2)
G0 X34
G0 Z-71.5
G1 X30 Z-71.5 F0.025
...
G1 X0 Z-71.5 F0.025
```

In the same program the groove finish passes show the convention since #641: the posted Z is the blade's -Z corner. The 2.5 mm O-ring groove Z -33.75..-36.25 is cut with the 2 mm blade at Z -36.25 and -35.75 (blade spans -36.25..-33.75, exact), and the 3 mm relief Z -17..-20 at Z -20 and -19. So the part-off blade at Z -71.5 spans **Z -71.5..-68.5**: it cuts 1.5 mm into the finished part's back face and removes the head chamfer. The part comes off 68.5 mm long instead of 70.

`verify` reports no warning for the operation (the lathe stock sim does not judge turning: "a turning program is cut by the field eye about its fitted spindle ... not judged here; the revolved verdict at generation stands"). The workaround the agent tried, `bottom_z` = bottom of model - 1.5, is refused: "nothing to part - the parting plane stands off the end of the bar" (the bar runs 14 mm further).

## Expected

The part-off blade's +Z flank stands at or behind the part's end plane (posted -Z corner at Z -73.0 for this 3 mm blade), or the operation is refused; a part-off that cuts into the part is a gouge and holds the post.

## Repro files

[q03-turn-shaft.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.camproj), [q03-turn-shaft.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.step), posted [q03-turn-shaft.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.nc) (lines 1610-1626 and 1716-1732 for the groove convention, 1813-1858 for the part-off); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/REPORT.md) problem 1.

The Tormach 24R machine file states no coolants. A user who sets an operation's coolant to **Off** (the right choice on a dry router) cannot post:

```
post: post blocked - 1 warning(s): operation F: asks off coolant, but this post script does not declare coolantModes (it does not read PARAM Coolant) - set the operation's coolant to Flood or use a post that reads it
```

Set back to **Flood**, the same program posts (65 lines) with no M7/M8/M9 at all, because tormach.cps treats an unstated coolant list as silent. So the refused setting and the accepted one give the same G-code, and the user is told to pick Flood on a machine without coolant. `verify` says `ok: true` before the post refuses.

Repro (MCP): `import_model` any part, `load_machine {"builtin": "Tormach 24R"}`, `fit_stock`, `add_tool {"catalog": "Router up-cut 6 mm"}`, `add_operation {"kind": "face", ...}`, `set_operation_coolant {"coolant": "off"}`, `generate`, `post {"post": "Tormach PathPilot", ...}`.

## Expected

On a machine whose coolant list is empty (or that states no Flood), Off posts: it writes no coolant word, which is what the post writes for Flood there anyway. Related but different: #3124 (hobby router files start new operations on Flood).

## Repro files

[q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj), [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 10.

Done means: a Tormach 24R operation with Coolant Off posts through Tormach PathPilot with no coolant word (pinned by a post test), and Flood on a machine with no coolant list either still posts silently or says so in the post notes.

## What happens

The part is a plate 160 x 70 x 15 mm (R8 corners) with a 140 x 50 x 4 mm centred pocket and two Ø6 through holes at X = ±70 (on the pocket wall). A 2D Contour, side **outside**, picked on the outer chain, top = top of model, bottom = bottom of model (Z 0), stepdown 3, 4 tabs, Router up-cut 6 mm, generates with `status: ok`, `warnings: 0` and only this note:

depth: the ring at (72.067, -37.999) ends at its floor Z 7.061 - the part is solid below it; levels below skipped (6.000, 3.000, 2.000, 0.000)

The point (72.067, -37.999) is 3 mm outside the plate edge (Y = -35), the tool-centre ring. Nothing of the part is below it. With `stock_to_leave: 0.02` the false floor moves by exactly +0.02 (Z 7.081 at (72.067, -38.019)). Same result with `tab_count: 0` and with the bottom outer chain picked.

The generate also takes 133 s for this one contour (re-run on len, 8 cores; the agent saw 3-6 min, so its MCP calls timed out at 3 min).

The contour cuts every level down to Z 0 and makes the 4 tabs, or names a real reason the levels are skipped as a warning, not an ok status.

title: Fanuc inch post can write a full-circle G03 for a short arc

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The native `post` command accepts two short counterclockwise arcs and writes two G03 blocks with coincident start and end XY coordinates. Both blocks have a nonzero center offset. A control that treats these blocks as full circles can cut a circle instead of a short stroke.

I reproduced this with CamCraft `post 0.25.0 (boa_engine)` and the original `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`. The post, CL reader and post script match main at `b44a422bb`. I checked the generated file. No controller or machine ran it.

## Reproduce

Save the following synthetic input as `tiny.cnc`. The coordinates in the intermediate file use micrometres.

```
; HSMW-CNC v1
PARAM OperationName Arc precision witness
PARAM SpindleSpeed 6000
PARAM WorkOffset 1
PARAM OriginX 0
PARAM OriginY 0
PARAM OriginZ 0
PARAM ToolDiameter 4
PARAM ClearancePlane 18
PARAM RetractPlane 18
PARAM TopOfStock 6
TOOL 1 EM-0400-2FL
SECTION Arc precision witness
Rapid X 18123 Y 5432 Z 18000
Plunge X 18123 Y 5432 Z 5500 F 45000
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5433 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5434 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Rapid X 18123 Y 5434 Z 18000
ENDSECTION
```

Run `cargo run -p camcraft-post --bin post -- --units inch assets/posts/fanuc.cps tiny.cnc tiny.nc`.

The input Y positions are 5432, 5433 and 5434 µm. Each arc has a sweep of about 0.00716°. In the NC file, the preceding position and both arc endpoints are X0.7135 Y0.2139. Each arc reads:

```text
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
```

The command exited successfully. It reported 13 mapped records, nine blocks and zero swallowed records.

## Expected

The post must preserve the short motion at the selected precision or refuse it with a diagnostic. It must distinguish a short arc from an intended full turn. Pin this input through the native post command. Also check a representable short arc and a genuine full circle.

Found while testing #1869. A check in the new sketch generator protects that feature. The native post also accepts intermediate files from other sources. #2191 concerned the radius-word mode and a different rounding failure.

Suggested labels are `bug`, `P1`, `area:post`, `effort:high`, and `source:agent`.

Found by QA brief q08 (AI chat panel with a local model) on v0.25.0 (7e2a8119), Linux x86_64, preset "Offline local (Ollama)", model qwen3-coder:latest.

**What happens:** in a fresh chat on a document with two operations, the request "Delete every operation." made the model call `delete_operation` twice ("Pocket roughing", "Pocket finishing"). Both calls ran at once - cards "Succeeded", no "Confirmation required" banner, no Allow/Deny. The document lost every operation. One Undo (ribbon) brought both back, so nothing was lost for good.

**Why:** `requires_confirmation` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/transport.rs` only asks in Native mode for `open_project` and for the live gate's kinds (`requires_approval` in `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`: post, file paths and writes, machine and limit edits). Destructive document edits (`delete_operation`, `delete_tool`, `delete_setup`, `delete_model`, ...) are never confirmed. The q08 brief and issue 3411 ("delete every operation (confirmation gate holds)") both expect a confirmation or a refusal here.

**Expected:** a delete (at least of operations, tools, setups or models) asked for by the model stops at the inline Allow/Deny banner, like `post` does; Deny sends "User denied tool ..." back to the model and changes nothing. One banner per turn for several deletes is fine.

**Evidence** (fork branch `qa-artifacts`, run q08-20261122T131017Z):
- panel after the turn: https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/28-step6b.png

- project to reproduce: https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/q08-after-step5.camproj

**Repro:** `camcraft-ui q08-after-step5.camproj`, Panels > AI Chat, provider "Offline local (Ollama)", model `qwen3-coder:latest`, prompt "Delete every operation." (any model that calls `delete_operation` will do; a scripted transport in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ai_chat/` reproduces it without a model).

title: chore(process): merge-ready and needs-rework never coexist on a PR

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

## The rule today
`AGENTS.md`, "Only collaborators' reviews count": a PR whose current head has a collaborator's change request and also `merge-ready` (or `merge-ready` with `needs-rework`) is a disagreement. `/merge-ready` reports it. "No agent removes a label. The two collaborators decide on the PR."

## The new rule
1. `merge-ready` and `needs-rework` are never on the same PR.
2. The person or agent that sets one of the two labels removes the other label in the same step, with one comment that says why.
3. A disagreement between two collaborators on the same head: `needs-rework` stays and `merge-ready` is removed. An open change request wins. The collaborator who set `merge-ready` gets the comment.
4. This replaces the text "No agent removes a label" for these two labels.

## Files to change
- `AGENTS.md`: the rule "Only collaborators' reviews count" (the disagreement items) and the "Review labels" table.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and the `PR-reviewer` agent file, where they set a review label.
- `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md`
- Each other skill or agent file that cites the old disagreement text (search for `needs-rework` and `disagreement`).

## Done means
- The files above state the new rule with the same words in each place.
- No file keeps the old text for these two labels.
- The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- If an `xtask` test pins the old text, the test changes with it.

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

Part of #3351. Refs #3351. This is sub-issue 1 of the plan in the research comments of #3351 (option C, the hybrid shape model).

## What to do

Add one internal shape type in `camcraft-tools`: the tool meridian. It is the cutting outline `rho(z)`, tip up, made of lines and circular arcs. All consumers read the tool shape through it in later sub-issues.

1. A new module (for example `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`, under 400 lines). It holds the meridian type and `Tool::meridian()`. Reuse the point form of `SpunProfile` (`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `z`, `r`, signed `arc`).
2. `Tool::meridian()` gives the meridian of each existing mill kind from its numbers: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Taper`, `Drill`, and the undercut heads of #1444 (`Lollipop`, `Dovetail`, `TSlot`, `Keyseat`). It agrees with `Tool::profile` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:387-465`) on the cutting band.
3. A split of the meridian into convex atoms:
   - a straight segment gives a frustum (each slope);
   - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
   - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (outer bound) or tangent frusta (inner bound), with a sag limit as a parameter.
4. Each atom carries a flag: cutting, or non-cutting (a pilot bearing band).
5. Degenerate input (a zero-length segment, a negative radius, a non-finite value, an arc that does not fit its chord) gives a named error. It never panics.

No consumer changes in this issue. No toolpath, simulation or check changes.

## Rules

- The geometry is from elementary plane geometry (chord sag `R (1 - cos(theta / 2))`) and convexity (Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, 3.2.5). Each module has its provenance line. No HSMWorks material.
- `effort:max`: a new geometry algorithm and the shape law that the gouge checks will read.

## Done means

- `Tool::meridian()` exists for each mill kind listed above.
- Tests pin, for each existing kind, that its convex atoms are the same solids that `Cutter::atoms` (`crates/sim/src/verify/probe.rs:180-230`) builds today, within 1e-9 mm.
- Tests pin the outer and inner bounds of a concave arc: the outer union contains the arc, the inner union stays inside it, and each sag is under the limit.
- Tests pin a named error for each degenerate input.

title: Do not touch: support Engrave operations

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab (Boundaries) does not work on a Engrave operation. The group shows only the note "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". There is no "Pick protected" button. The maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations, in his words: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs" (#2055).

Found during the work on #3335. Refs #2055. Refs #3335.

## What to do

1. Add `OpType::Engrave` to `do_not_touch_applies` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`).
2. Make the Engrave generator keep the full tool (flutes, shank and holder) clear of each protected face and edge, by the clearance. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges.
3. If the generator cannot keep clear, refuse the operation or mark it "incomplete". The diagnostic names the item. The post is blocked.
4. The verify check and the post gate already check the protected items. Make sure that they read the Engrave moves.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor: it changes the toolpath and the posted G-code of a Engrave operation that has protected items. A Engrave operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before. Pin that.

## Done means

- The Boundary group of a Engrave operation shows "Pick protected", and a viewport click adds a face or an edge row.
- A test with a protected face next to the cut shows that no move comes nearer than the clearance.
- A test with a protected face that the cut cannot avoid shows the refusal with the item named, and a blocked post.
- A test shows that a Engrave operation without protected items gives the same toolpath.

title: Boundaries: one Boundary offset moves both the picked edge and the outer boundary - they need separate offsets

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; boundaries; we should have control over how much the "outside boundary" offset is and the "inside boundary" offset is.. now its just boundary offset, which when i shrink it to a negative value also offsets the boundary from the face/edge i picked. Which makes it problematic to control the boundaries using the strategies choosen for example "Open-Machine side B". generates a very generous outside boundary that makes you cut air for a good halv a minute.

## What happens

The Boundary group has one row, "Boundary offset" (`AreaControls::offset`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs:86`; row in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:114`). Its hint says: "+ grows the area outward, - shrinks it inward". The one value moves the whole area edge: the edge that the user picked (the face or the edge chain) and the outer boundary (the stock outline that an open boundary runs on to).

The user wants the outer boundary to be tighter. He sets a negative offset. The picked edge moves as well, so the area no longer starts at the face or edge that he picked. He cannot get both.

## The cost

With "Open - machine side B" the area is the part between the picked chain and the stock outline. The outer boundary is "very generous". The tool cuts air for about half a minute. The user has no way to shrink only that outer side.

## Expected

Two offsets, each with its own row and hint:

1. Offset of the picked edge or face (the inside boundary): moves the line that the user picked. Default 0.
2. Offset of the outer boundary (the outside boundary: the stock outline, or the open boundary's run-on): moves only that line. Default 0.

Each one applies to a closed boundary and an open boundary. A closed boundary that has only the picked loop uses the first one. The "Extend past open edges" value is separate, as it is now.

## Rules

- The default of both is 0 and the output is byte-identical for a project that has one `offset` value of 0. A project with a non-zero `offset` loads as the same value in BOTH new offsets: the output stays the same (project-file version bump and a migration test).
- The change is an undoable command (`EditOperationParams`). The MCP tool gets both fields.
- The region and the verify check read the same two values. The planner never refuses the picked line because the outer offset is negative.
- Safety floor: this changes the machined region. The pin goes red first, the review is an independent Opus read, and the heavy lanes that the diff reaches run.

## Done means

- A pin test: an open boundary, side B, on a model with a stock larger than the part. With the outer offset negative and the picked offset 0, the region edge on the picked chain stays on the chain, and the outer edge moves in. The cut-air length drops by the measured amount.
- A structural test of the two rows (labels, hints, default).
- The project-file migration test and a byte-identical golden for an old project.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> Bug; the "do not touch" feature under boundaries, should allow me to pick a face or an edge. But i does not..

He did not say which operation kind he used, or what happens on a click. The worker finds this first.

## What the code says

The feature is #2055 (closed). The wanted behaviour: the "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab lets the user click faces and edges in the viewport. Each pick shows as a row with a remove button.

Two readings of the report. The worker checks both:

1. The group is not usable for the operation kind that the maintainer uses. `do_not_touch_unsupported` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs:54`) says: "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". For each other kind the group shows only that sentence. There is no "Pick protected" button (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:305-314`). The wording "clear it on {kind}" does not say how to pick, and the group still shows in the Boundaries area where the user expects a pick control.
2. The group is usable (2D Offset, 3D Pocket), but the viewport click does not fill it. The click path is `take_pick` -> `take_do_not_touch_pick` (`crates/ui/src/boundary_draft.rs:355-398`). A click may go to the selection and not to the group, for example when a vertex is hit (the code ignores vertices), or when the group is in the "Picking…" state but another pick tool holds the viewport.

## Expected

- For each operation kind that has the group, a click on a face or an edge adds a row to "Do not touch". The status line says what was added.
- For a kind that does not support it, the user sees why, in plain words, and what to do. The better answer is to support the kind (the maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations in #2055: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs").

## Done means

- A structural test in `crates/ui`: with the group open, a face click and an edge click each add one row; a remove click takes it away; the status line names the pick.
- The worker names the operation kind and the exact reason in a comment on this issue. If the cause is reading 1, the worker files one sub-issue per kind that lacks the feature (`Refs #2055`, bug, P3, source:agent, effort by the table; the safety floor applies to the generator work).
- The change goes through the same undoable command and MCP tool as the existing "Do not touch" picks.

title: Start and exit points: the shared mechanism (design decision)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448.

## Why

The maintainer set the scope of #1448 on 2026-11-22: a user-set start point and exit point on EVERY operation that cuts a path. He asked for one shared mechanism: one command, one MCP tool, one viewport pick, one pair of rows. He set it to `bug` and `P2`: "Mark them as P2 - they are bugs at this point".

Today only the closed 2D Contour rings take a start point and an exit point. The kind table is in the research comment on #1448. Each family sub-issue of #1448 depends on this issue.

The shared design is recorded in `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` before the next slice (comment on #1448, 2026-11-22).

## What `main` has

- `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/motion/src/approach.rs:162,168`): `Option<Point2>`, model XY in mm, inside `links.approach`.
- Kinds with a `links` field: Contour, Pocket, Adaptive2D, Offset2D, Circular, Slot, Pocket3D, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Bore. The other 33 path kinds have no `links`.
- The project keys `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/app/src/project/approach.rs:77,81`). The digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` (`crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs:202-212`).
- `EditOperationParams` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs`). `named_refusal` runs at create, edit and load (`sane.rs:54`).
- MCP: the generic patch of `edit_operation` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:304-318`). The schema does not name the fields.
- UI: `start_exit_rows.rs` and `start_exit_pick.rs`, only on the 2D Contour lead tab (`approach_page.rs:140-182`).
- A second, separate start field: `WireContourOp.start` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:61-63`).

## Open questions, options and the recommended option

### 1. One shared type

- A: Keep the fields in `links.approach`, and add `links` to each kind that has none.
- B: A new shared type in `camcraft-motion`, for example `PathPicks { start, exit }`. Every path kind holds it. One accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` reads it for every kind. The contour moves its two fields into it. Wire Contour moves `start` into it.
- C: A field for each kind.

Recommended: B. Option A gives `links` to kinds that have no links (turning, EDM, plasma), and the field has no meaning there. Option C repeats the refusal law 43 times.

Sub-question: the shape of a pick. Today it is a 2D point. A 3D finishing start, a multi-axis start and a turning (Z, X) start need more. Recommended: a pick holds a model-frame point with an optional Z. Each family projects it in its own frame (setup XY, the tilted frame, the lathe (Z, X) plane). Sub-question: one pick for each operation, or one for each chain or region (the #1448 body says "one pick per chain or region"). Recommended: the type holds a list from the first slice, so that the file format does not change again. A first slice can refuse a list longer than one by name.

### 2. The project key

- A: Keep `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point`.
- B: A new key at the operation level (for example `picks: { start: [...], exit: [...] }`). The loader also reads the old `links.approach.*` keys and the old wire `start` key, so every saved file opens unchanged.

Recommended: B, with the old keys read on load. The digest keeps `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values, so a contour golden does not change.

### 3. The command

- A: `EditOperationParams`, as today.
- B: A dedicated `SetStartExit` command.

Recommended: A. One undo step can then change the pick and the "Pass starts at" option of #3316 together. The maintainer asked for one command.

### 4. The MCP tool

- A: The generic patch of `edit_operation`, as today, with the fields named in its schema.
- B: A dedicated tool, for example `set_start_exit`.

Recommended: A, with the fields named in the schema of `edit_operation` and a read-only answer (in the kind description) that says which kinds take a pick. Option B gives two doors to one command.

### 5. The viewport pick and the rows

- Recommended: one capability for each kind in `KindInfo` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`), for example `Ring`, `Region`, `HoleOrder`, `Ends`, `Raster`, `NotTaken(reason)`.
- The pick snaps by capability: a wall for `Ring`, a point inside the region for `Region`, a hole for `HoleOrder`, an end for `Ends`, a corner for `Raster`.
- The rows of `start_exit_rows.rs` move to a shared group. Every operation page draws it.
- A kind with `NotTaken` draws the row with the reason by name (the maintainer: "Where a kind has no free start, the Start point row says so by name").

### 6. How the path is generated again to the point

- The pick is an input of the planner. The command changes the parameters. The normal generate runs after it, as for the contour today.
- Recommended: promote the ring helpers of `contour_start.rs` (`nearest_on_ring`, `reach`, `lead_held`) to a shared module in `crates/motion/src/`, for every ring and chain family.
- Each family keeps its own seam: re-sequence a ring, place the descent in a region, order the holes, choose an end, choose a raster corner.

### 7. Beside "Pass starts at" of #3316

- #3316 adds one shared parameter "Pass starts at: Auto / Inside / Outside" and its decision file `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`. This issue does not change it.
- The two choices work together. The pass side chooses which ring of a level cuts first. The start point chooses the place on that ring, and the descent place.
- Recommended order: the planner applies the pass side first, then projects the start pick onto the first ring that the pass side gives.
- A pick that the pass side makes impossible is refused by name. Example: "Outside" with a start pick inside the part.
- The design file names `3316-pass-start-shared.md` and keeps the two parameters as two fields in the same parameter group.

### 8. The refusal when a point cannot be reached

- A: Refuse by name (the contour law today).
- B: Move the pick to the nearest legal point and add a warning.

Recommended: A. The maintainer: "a pick is a wish. The planner refuses it by name when the lead law or the safety laws cannot hold it. It never moves the pick without a note."

Where each refusal runs:
- At command creation (`named_refusal`): the kind does not take a pick, the pick is not finite, or the pick is outside the setup.
- At generation: no lead fits, the helix does not fit, the pick is too far from the path, the pick conflicts with the pass side. The operation is refused, and the post is blocked.

Each message names the operation kind, the pick (start or exit), the reason and the user's next step.

## Done means

- `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` records each answer above: the choice, the reason and the dropped options.
- The shared type, the project key with the read of the old keys, the `edit_operation` schema fields, the `KindInfo` capability and the shared row group are on `main`.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key.
- No family planner change is in this issue. The family sub-issues of #1448 do that.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> Bug, hiding world origin axis, should not hide world plane/grid, that should hide seperatly.

## What happens

The user turns off the world origin axes. The viewport grid (the world plane) disappears as well. The user has no way to hide the axes and keep the grid.

## Expected

Two separate switches. "Origin axes" hides the axes only. "Grid" hides the grid only.

## What the code says

- The Display menu has two boxes: "Grid" (`show_grid`) and "Origin axes" (`show_world_axes`) in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/display_menu.rs`. The Browser pane has a third switch, "Show world origin axes" (`browser_pane.rs`), and the viewport bar has a fourth, the axes toggle (`viewport_bar.rs`). All three write `show_world_axes`.
- The grid is drawn only when both flags are on: `if !state.show_world_axes || !state.show_grid { return ... }` in `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`. The comment there says that the grid uses the same switch as the triads. The doc comment of `show_grid` in `state.rs` says that the grid also needs `show_world_axes`.
- The test `egui_app::tests::display_menu` checks only one direction: with the grid hidden, the axes stay. It does not check the other direction.
- The issue #2818 (closed) added the "Grid" box. It was written so that the box "hides the grid alone". It did not make the axes switch independent of the grid.

## Fix

The grid depends on `show_grid` only. The axes depend on `show_world_axes` only. Update the two comments. Add a test: with the axes hidden and the grid on, the grid is drawn.

## Not changed

The saved view preferences keep both keys. A project that hid the axes before shows the grid again after the change. Say this in the changelog row.

Done means: a structural test shows the grid drawn with the axes off, and the axes drawn with the grid off, from each of the three switches; the comments are correct.

labels.name: source:agent

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> if we look at the lead in and lead out.. the between levels happens at clearance plane.. and between passes happens at retract plane. but i cannot see a retract plane

## What happens

The Lead in / Lead out tab of a 2D Offset operation has two link rows:
- "Between levels" is set to "Clearance plane".
- "Between passes" is set to "Retract plane".

The Heights tab has no Retract Z row. Its Levels group has only "Hop below clearance" (off) and "Stepdown". The viewport labels three planes: Clearance (32.00, stock top +10), Top (22.00) and Bottom (1.50). It labels no retract plane. So the user cannot see or edit the plane that "Between passes" says it uses.

## What the code says

- The hint of the Heights tab says: "the retract plane: on, links hop at Retract Z; off, every link climbs to Clearance Z" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/heights_page.rs`). The Retract Z row exists only while "Hop below clearance" is on.
- The Lead tab lists "Clearance plane / Retract plane / Keep down" for each link (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs`). It does not say which height "Retract plane" means when the hop is off.
- The user guide says that a kind that has one gets a retract plane 10 above the stock top (`operations-2d.md`).

## Not known yet

Which height the generator uses for a link set to "Retract plane" when "Hop below clearance" is off, for 2D Offset. The hint of the Heights tab suggests the clearance height. The Lead tab suggests a separate plane. The worker reads the generator and says which one is true.

## Expected

One of these, and the maintainer chooses:
- "Retract plane" is shown on the Heights tab and in the viewport whenever a link uses it, with its value.
- Or the choice is hidden or renamed while no retract plane exists.

The Lead tab then never offers a plane that the user cannot see.

## Related

title: 2D Offset with Outside containment: the passes start inside and cut from the inside out, so the tool slots in the stock

labels.name: bug

labels.name: effort:max

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; Movement calcualtion; P2; Example 2D offset set with a outside continment, helixes dowwn inside of the calculated "containmen" and works its way from the inside out.. Which ends up being fully engagend slotting movements not following the rules where it should have been starting outside the part and worked itself in. We might need to add a option prob. undder "passes", that stats "Pass starts at <auto, inside, outside>".. where Auto is current behavior for setting it up and the other two forces either or. So we get control over the fact that it should not try to crate slots in the stock

## What happens

A 2D Offset operation has the containment "Outside". The tool helixes down inside the calculated containment. It then cuts the passes from the inside out. The result is fully engaged slotting moves in the stock.

## Expected

An "Outside" containment starts outside the part and works inward. The tool never makes a fully engaged slot in the stock.

## The change that the maintainer suggests

A new option on the Passes tab: "Pass starts at", with the values Auto, Inside and Outside.
- Auto keeps the current behaviour.
- Inside and Outside force the order.

The user then controls the order and stops the slots. This follows the rule that a strategy fork is an operation parameter with a default.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119 (built 2026-11-22 02:53 UTC). The maintainer sent a screenshot. It is not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8 end mill), model `fig8`, setup `Setup1`, machine VMC 3-AXIS, post Siemens 840D.
- The status line reads `OK - 8318 moves - 1 warning`. The warning reads: "feed moves 686 and 836 cross in XY at shared depth - repeated on 4 more moves (to 7496)". The operation tree shows 5 warnings.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: Entry type Helix, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Level to level "Same as entry", Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane".
- The simulation at 60.7 / 1392.8 s shows the tool deep inside the machined area. The cut area around it is a closed slot.
- The maintainer's project file is a local file. Use the tracked model `testdata/models/fig8.step` and the tool `EM-0800-4FL` to reproduce.

## Possible link (not checked)

#2849, test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) uses the same model, the same tool and an "Outside" containment. Its body says that the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline, and the PR #3267 says that a ring order change fixes it but turns `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. The two pins want opposite ring orders. A parameter for the order may settle both. The worker checks if this is the same defect and says so on both issues.

## Safety

A fully engaged slot overloads the tool. The toolpath is not a silent wrong cut, but it is a toolpath that the user must not run. If the fix changes pass order or the posted moves, it is under the safety floor: the pin goes red first, and the review is an independent Opus read with a hand trace.

Done means: a pin test shows an Outside containment that starts outside and cuts inward on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL`, with no move whose engagement is a full slot; the new option and its three values are in the property panel and in MCP; Auto keeps the current output of all shipped goldens.

title: OBJ import refuses valid face indices after duplicate vertices

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:3d

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## What happens

The OBJ importer refuses a legal face after duplicate vertex records.
I found this while building the five-axis example for #2870.

This OBJ has six vertex records. The second face refers to records 4, 5, and 6.

```obj
v -24 12 0
v -24 11 4
v -16 11 4
f 1 2 3
v -24 12 0
v -16 11 4
v -16 12 0
f 4 5 6
```

The importer reports `vertex reference '5' out of range`.
It must preserve the original vertex indices when it resolves each face.

## Cause

On upstream/main d911f455, `crates/app/src/geometry/import/obj.rs` removes duplicate vertex records before it resolves face indices.
The face handler uses the shortened vertex list.

## Workaround

Write each vertex once. Use its index in that unique list.
The generator for #2870 uses this workaround.

## Done means

The importer accepts the example and preserves both triangles.
Tests cover positive and negative indices after duplicate vertex records.
Malformed references still give a clear error.

effort:high - The fix changes imported geometry. The safety floor applies.

Found while working #2870. Catalog umbrella: #2392.

title: ui: an UndercutLift warning can hide a "Do not touch" hit on avoid part 1 (fold key 217)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Same class as #3040. `fold_warnings_located` (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs`) groups warnings by a numeric key, and a group prints only the line of its first warning. `Warning::AvoidHit { part, .. }` uses `216 + part`, so the range is 216..=220. `Warning::UndercutLift` (Slot Undercut, commit 5452810e5, 2026-11-19) uses **217**, the key of an `AvoidHit` on part 1. When the undercut lift comes first, the blocking "Do not touch" hit on part 1 folds into the advisory as "repeated on N more moves" and is not shown.

#3040 / PR #3062 moves `DrillUndersize` from 216 to 223 and expected `UndercutLift` at 222 (PR #2836's plan). Keys in use on main: 221 is `FirstTraverseLow` and 224 is `FirstTraverseUnderTable`, so 222 is free.

Done means: `UndercutLift` folds under a key outside 216..=220 that no other warning uses (222), and a pinning test folds one `UndercutLift` and one `AvoidHit` on part 1 and asserts both lines are shown, like `a_drill_undersize_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` in #3062.

| 44948384882 | 273642212 | skull | `ui suites: lib` | 20:50-22:15 |

title: ci(cut): give cut.yml its own runner label so the release gate cannot land on a post-merge runner

labels.name: area:build

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
`cut.yml` runs both its jobs on `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`. GitHub matches labels case-insensitively, and every post-merge runner is registered with `self-hosted,Linux,X64,camcraft-post-merge`. Since 2026-11-21 there are eight of them. So the release gate (up to 5 h, sized for 16 cores and 64 GB) can land on any of them, including 8-thread laptops and 24 GB boxes. The PR-test runner `len` once took a cut job the same way (2026-11-14).

For the cut of 2026-11-21, a stop-gap on the runner owner's side stops every runner except `wopr` while a release PR is open.

## Change
- `.github/workflows/cut.yml`: both `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` become `runs-on: [self-hosted, camcraft-cut]`.
- AGENTS.md and `.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md`: the cut runner carries the label `camcraft-cut`.

## Merge order (important)
Merge only **after** a runner has the `camcraft-cut` label: Settings -> Actions -> Runners -> `wopr` -> add label `camcraft-cut` (optionally `uma` as a backup). No re-registration is needed. If `cut.yml` asks for the label before any runner has it, the gate waits in the queue forever. Never merge it during a cut.

Done means: `cut.yml` targets `camcraft-cut`, the docs name it, at least one runner carries the label, and the next cut's gate runs there.

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

title: contour: the refusal for a non-centre-cutting tool with Arc entry and no lead-in gives a misleading hint
