body:
Found in the second safety read of PR #3140 (comment 7069305890).

After PR #3140, a Contour with Arc entry and both leads set to None stands the wall arc down. The level then descends straight down. With a tool that is not centre-cutting, the operation is refused. The refusal is correct and safe. But its hint tells the user to "pick the Arc entry", and the user already has Arc entry.

Expected: the hint names the real cause. The lead-in is None, so the arc entry does not run. The user can set a Linear or Arc lead-in, or use a centre-cutting tool.

The PR body of #3140 calls this a "wording follow-up". This issue tracks it. Change only the message text and its test. The refusal must stay.

title: 2D Chamfer: add progressive passes across the chamfer width

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer currently cuts the full requested chamfer in one pass.

The operation calculates the final depth from the requested width and angle. It then runs the selected closed or open path at that one depth.

A single pass can apply a large cutting load to a chamfer mill. It can also reduce finish quality on a deep chamfer or on a difficult material.

Users need to distribute the chamfer over several progressive passes:

- The first pass makes a small chamfer.
- Later passes increase the chamfer width.
- The final pass reaches the authored width.
- The final part geometry remains unchanged.

This feature must not create several parallel paths at the same depth. Each pass must advance to a larger chamfer width and its matching derived depth.

## Meaning of passes

In this issue, **passes** means progressive chamfer passes across the width.

It does not mean generic Z stepdown. The Chamfer depth comes from the horizontal width and the cone angle. A separate Z stepdown could break the required cone-to-face contact.

It does not model physical tool-tip diameter, flat length, or radius. That work belongs to #895.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` holds one final `width`.
- The generator derives one `break_depth` from `width * tan(angle)`.
- The generator derives one virtual-tip Z.
- The motion uses one Z level.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Passes** tab.
- The operation records one `EdgeBreak`.
- A one-pass path defines the current compatibility output.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Passes** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add one field:

| Field | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Number of passes | 1 | 1–100 | The number of progressive chamfer passes |

Tooltip:

> The operation cuts progressive chamfer widths from the first pass to the final pass. The final pass creates the complete requested width.

A value of `1` keeps the current behavior.

Do not add a raw Z stepdown field. The user controls the final width and the pass count. The generator derives each pass depth.

## Pass-width rule

Let:

- `w` be the final authored chamfer width.
- `n` be the number of passes.
- `i` be the current pass number, starting at 1.
- `a` be the chamfer angle in degrees.
- `r` be the tip offset from #3153.

Each pass uses:

```text
pass width i = w × i / n
```

For a final width of `2 mm` and two passes:

```text
pass 1 width = 1 mm
pass 2 width = 2 mm
```

For four passes:

```text
0.5 mm
1.0 mm
1.5 mm
2.0 mm
```

The sequence always starts at the smallest width and ends at the final width.

## Depth rule

The final authored break depth remains:

```text
final depth = w × tan(a)
```

Each progressive pass uses:

```text
pass depth i = pass width i × tan(a)
```

The virtual cone-tip Z for each pass is:

```text
tip Z i = Top Z - (r + pass width i) × tan(a)
```

The tip offset stays constant through the sequence.

The operation changes the cone depth for each pass. It does not move the cutter axis farther from the selected edge on each pass.

## Pass transition

The base implementation uses a safe retract between passes.

Each pass follows this order:

1. Enter on the air side.
2. Cut the complete selected path at the pass depth.
3. Leave on the air side.
4. Retract to the retract or clearance plane.
5. Move to the next pass.
6. Enter at the next progressive depth.

The operation must not plunge directly from one chamfer depth to the next.

The lead rules from #3237 apply to each pass when that issue is available. Before #3237, the implementation must preserve the safe open-chain approach and exit from #2988.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Passes run from the shallowest width to the final width.
- Each pass follows the selected climb direction.
- Each pass starts and ends at a valid seam.
- The operation cuts one complete loop for each pass.
- A one-pass operation keeps the exact current point order.
- Pass transitions do not create another finished edge break.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Every pass enters and exits on the physical air side.
- The final pass covers the complete selected chain.
- The cone-offset side classification remains valid at every pass depth.
- A pass that reaches model material on the air side is refused.
- A short, folded, or missing offset remains a refusal.
- The refusal names the pass and the endpoint that failed.

## Edge-break rule

Only the final pass represents the finished authored chamfer.

Record one `EdgeBreak` for each selected source path:

- The edge remains the original selected edge.
- The width remains the authored final width.
- The depth remains `w × tan(a)`.
- The slope remains `tan(a)`.
- Intermediate passes do not receive separate `EdgeBreak` records.

Stock simulation and collision checks still evaluate every generated pass motion.

This rule prevents intermediate roughing passes from receiving full finished-chamfer credit.

## Tool and safety checks

The final pass must pass the existing checks:

- The tool must be a supported chamfer mill.
- The operation angle must match the tool cone.
- The active tool radius must cover `r + w`.
- The tool flute reach must cover `(r + w) × tan(a)`.
- Every pass width must be finite, positive, and increasing.
- The cone envelope must stay safe for every pass.
- Every retract and pass transition must remain clear of the model.

The implementation may use the final pass for monotonic radius and flute-reach limits. It must still verify the actual swept motion of every pass.

The implementation must refuse:

- A pass count outside 1–100.
- More levels than the shared maximum-pass budget allows.
- Non-finite calculated widths or depths.
- A pass transition that enters model material.
- An air-side cone sweep that reaches model material.

The diagnostic must name the selected chain, pass number, conflict location, and safe correction.

## Feed behavior

Each progressive pass uses the Chamfer cutting feed.

This issue does not add:

- A roughing feed.
- A finishing feed.
- A feed reduction for the first pass.
- A separate feed for pass links.

## Proposed fix

1. Add a pass count to the 2D Chamfer operation parameters.
2. Add the pass count to the project parameter DTO.
3. Add the pass count to MCP operation create, edit, read, and job-description output.
4. Show the field on the 2D Chamfer **Passes** tab.
5. Generate cumulative widths from the first pass to the final pass.
6. Derive each pass depth from width and angle.
7. Derive each virtual-tip Z from tip offset and pass width.
8. Run the passes from the shallowest to the deepest.
9. Retract safely between passes.
10. Apply the lead rule from #3237 to each pass.
11. Keep one final `EdgeBreak` for each selected source path.
12. Reuse shared level or pass machinery only when its transition assumptions match Chamfer.
13. Update the operation guide, field help, and examples.

#1890 and PR #3220 provide prior art for progressive 3D Deburr passes. The 2D Chamfer implementation must use its own cone geometry, width law, and `EdgeBreak` law.

## Compatibility

A pass count of `1` must preserve:

- Point order.
- Z level.
- Entry and exit motion.
- Retract structure.
- Notes.
- `EdgeBreak` values.
- Existing CL and G-code goldens.

Old projects must read an absent pass count as `1`.

The default value must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes. Old readers must reject a project with more than one pass after the project-format version changes.

New readers must load old one-pass projects.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Generic Chamfer stepdown.
- Constant-depth Chamfer mode.
- Stock to leave.
- Different roughing and finishing feed rates.
- Spring passes.
- Flat-tip, ball-tip, or radiused chamfer tools.
- Per-pass tip offset.
- User-selectable level or pass links.

## Dependencies

- #2988 and PR #3059 define selected open chains.
- #3153 defines tip offset.
- #3237 defines lead-in and lead-out.
- #895 defines real physical chamfer-tip geometry.

The implementation should complete after #2988 and #3153. It should reuse #3237 for safe entry and exit when #3237 is available.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- One pass is byte-equivalent to the current path.
- Two passes create increasing widths.
- A 45-degree, 2 mm final chamfer uses 1 mm and 2 mm pass widths.
- A 45-degree, four-pass chamfer uses evenly spaced progressive widths.
- Each pass depth equals `pass width × tan(angle)`.
- Each virtual-tip depth includes tip offset.
- Passes run from shallow to final depth.
- A transition retracts safely between passes.
- A closed path cuts every progressive pass once.
- An open chain enters and exits safely for every pass.
- #3237 lead settings apply to every pass.
- Only the final pass produces the finished `EdgeBreak`.
- Intermediate motion remains included in simulation and collision checks.
- Pass counts below 1 and above 100 are refused.
- The shared maximum-pass limit is enforced.
- The tool-radius refusal names the final limiting pass.
- The flute-reach refusal names the final limiting pass.
- Old projects read pass count as 1.
- A default project round-trip keeps the old bytes.
- MCP can create, edit, and read the pass count.
- The UI shows the field and tooltip.
- The guide describes the progressive-width and depth rules.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows a **Passes** tab.
- The user can select 1–100 progressive passes.
- The final pass reaches the authored chamfer width.
- Each pass depth follows the chamfer angle.
- Each virtual-tip depth follows the tip offset.
- The operation runs from the shallowest to the final pass.
- Transitions retract safely between passes.
- One pass preserves the current output.
- Only the final pass records a finished edge break.
- Focused motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The reached heavy lanes run on the final branch.
- The site guide documents the pass-width law.

Changelog: Add progressive passes to 2D Chamfer while preserving the final requested chamfer width.

title: 2D Chamfer: add configurable lead-in and lead-out

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer has no user control for lead-in or lead-out.

The operation lowers the tool at the first cut point and starts the chamfer immediately. This behavior can place the tool directly on a finished edge. It can also create visible tool marks at the start or end of a chamfer.

Open-chain support from #2988 adds a fixed air-side extension at each endpoint. That extension has no user-selected shape, length, radius, or feed behavior. It is not a complete lead feature.

Users need to:

- Start and finish a chamfer away from the final edge.
- Select a lead shape that fits the available air space.
- Use a tangential entry when a direct or perpendicular entry leaves a mark.
- Use a different lead-out when the end of the path has different clearance.
- Shorten a lead near a wall, fixture, or nearby part.
- Use the same lead concepts that 2D Contour already provides.

This issue separates three motions:

1. **Entry** moves in Z from a safe plane to the lead start.
2. **Lead-in** moves in XY and joins the chamfer path.
3. **Lead-out** moves in XY and leaves the chamfer path.

This issue adds lead-in and lead-out. It does not add ramp or helical entry.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` has no lead-in or lead-out values.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
- Closed paths enter at the selected seam and cut one circuit.
- Open paths receive fixed air-side extensions from #2988.
- The operation runs one chamfer path at one derived depth.
- The lead geometry is not persisted, exposed through MCP, or documented.

The 2D Contour lead model in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_params.rs` is useful prior art. Its `Lead` values are:

- `None`
- `Linear`
- `Arc`
- `Tangential`
- `Perpendicular`

Contour lead-fit logic also shrinks a lead when the requested shape does not fit. Chamfer needs stricter checks because the chamfer cone, not only a cutter centerline, moves through the lead.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Lead in / Lead out** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add these lead-in choices:

| Type | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| None | None | Start directly on the path. |
| Linear | Length | Enter behind the path tangent. |
| Arc | Radius | Join the path with a quarter arc. |
| Tangential | Radius | Join the path with a tangential semicircle. |
| Perpendicular | Length | Enter from the normal direction. |

Add these lead-out choices:

- Same as lead-in
- None
- Linear
- Arc
- Tangential
- Perpendicular

Show only the length or radius that the selected lead uses.

Use these defaults:

- Lead-in: `None`
- Lead-out: `Same as lead-in`

Old projects with no lead fields must read as `Lead::None`. A default operation must preserve the existing path.

## Motion order

The motion order for one selected chain is:

1. Rapid to the lead-start point.
2. Move in Z to the chamfer depth with the existing entry law.
3. Feed through the lead-in.
4. Cut the complete selected chamfer path.
5. Feed through the lead-out.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Move to the next chain or finish the operation.

The chamfer cutting feed controls each lead feed. This issue does not add a separate lead feed.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Lead-in starts on the air side at the selected seam.
- Lead-in joins the path at the seam.
- The operation runs the closed path once.
- Lead-out leaves from the same seam.
- The planner must prevent the lead-in and lead-out from crossing.
- The operation records the selected edge break once.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Lead-in and lead-out follow the physical air side at each endpoint.
- The planner reads the material side from the selected model.
- The planner does not infer the air side only from chain point order.
- Explicit `Side` must agree with the physical wall class.
- The fixed extension from #2988 moves under the new lead planner.
- A user selection of `None` adds no extra XY feed motion.
- A sharp turn near an endpoint must not receive an unsafe generic extension.

## Lead-fit rule

The implementation follows this order:

1. Build the requested lead.
2. Verify the complete cutter-cone sweep.
3. If the lead does not fit, halve its length or radius up to the existing lead-fit limit.
4. If a smaller lead fits, report the requested and used values in the operation notes.
5. If no safe lead fits, refuse the operation.

The operation must not silently replace an unsafe requested lead with `None`.

The refusal must name:

- The lead-in or lead-out that failed.
- The selected chain.
- The conflict location.
- The unavailable air space or material conflict.
- A useful correction, such as a shorter lead or a smaller radius.

## Cone safety rule

The lead check must verify the complete active cone envelope. It must not verify only the centerline or the virtual tip.

The check must include:

- Chamfer width.
- Cone angle.
- Tip offset from #3153.
- The full active cone band.
- The cutter body above the cone.
- The lead-to-path transition.
- The complete line or arc sweep.

A lead is legal only when that complete sweep stays on the air side and outside the model.

The generated lead must not:

- Cross selected model material.
- Enter through a finished face.
- Pass through another selected chain.
- Fold onto itself.
- Add finished geometry outside the selected edge.
- Add `EdgeBreak` credit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add persistent lead-in and lead-out values to the 2D Chamfer parameter model.
2. Reuse the existing `Lead` value family where the semantics match.
3. Add a Chamfer-specific lead planner.
4. Reuse Contour shape construction only where the mathematics match.
5. Derive the physical air side from the selected open or closed model boundary.
6. Sweep the complete cutter cone through every lead move.
7. Keep the existing Chamfer path when both leads use `None`.
8. Add the fields to project serialization and version migration.
9. Add the fields to MCP create, edit, read, and job-description output.
10. Show the controls in the 2D Chamfer **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
11. Update the operation guide and field help.

The implementation must not copy the Contour centerline room check and call it sufficient for Chamfer.

## Compatibility

- A default 2D Chamfer keeps the current closed-loop output.
- Old projects read absent lead fields as `None`.
- Old readers must reject non-default lead settings after the project-format version change.
- A `None` default must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes.
- The lead values must round-trip through project save and load.
- The lead values must round-trip through MCP.

## Related work

- #2988 and PR #3059 add selected open chains.
- #3153 adds tip offset.
- #895 models real flat, ball, or radiused chamfer-tool tips.
- #3132 and PR #3140 address a 2D Contour lead issue and remain separate.

This work must use the final chain and cone geometry from #2988 and #3153.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- A closed-loop path with `None` remains unchanged.
- Missing project fields read as `None`.
- Every lead shape produces the expected geometry.
- Lead-out can differ from lead-in.
- Lead direction follows the climb direction.
- A closed path uses the correct seam for both leads.
- Open-chain leads stay on the physical air side.
- A positive tip offset remains safe through the transition.
- An inside wall does not receive an outward lead.
- A self-crossing lead is refused.
- A material-crossing lead is refused.
- A lead that can fit only when smaller is shrunk and reported.
- A lead that cannot fit is refused.
- A lead adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- UI values round-trip through the operation.
- Project values round-trip through save and load.
- MCP can create, edit, and read each lead value.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Ramp or helical entry.
- A separate lead feed.
- User-selected retract or pass links.
- Multiple Chamfer passes.
- Real tool-tip radius or diameter.
- Stock-to-leave or finishing stock.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows lead-in and lead-out controls.
- All supported lead shapes generate deterministic motion.
- Open and closed paths use the physical air side.
- The complete cutter cone stays safe through every lead.
- Default and old projects preserve the previous path.
- No safe room produces an explicit refusal.
- Lead motion adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- Motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The site guide describes the new controls.

Changelog: Add configurable lead-in and lead-out moves to 2D Chamfer.

title: 3+2 under-table refusal gives heights in the tilted frame, not the value that the user typed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The refusal `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (#3081) gives two heights in the local frame of the 3+2 plane. The message calls them Z values. The user sets the clearance height in the user frame, so the numbers in the message are not values that the user can type.

Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`, `judge`). `table_read` returns `limit` as "a local height" (its doc comment), and `judge` puts `start_h` (also local) into `height_mm`. Nothing adds `origin.z` back before the message.

Example from `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`, `a_head_tilt_past_90_under_the_table_is_refused_with_lower`:

- The tilt origin is at Z 20 (`ORIGIN_Z`). The user sets the clearance height to 170 (`ORIGIN_Z + 150.0`). The head tilts to B 120.
- The message says: "to the clearance plane at Z150.000 it can go under the table top - lower the clearance plane to Z113.590 or under it".
- In the user frame, the plane is at 170 and the limit is 133.590.

The verdict is correct and the post stays blocked. Only the numbers and the word "Z" in the text are wrong:

- With `origin.z` > 0, a user who types the given limit gets a plane that is lower than necessary.
- With `origin.z` < 0, a user who types the given limit gets the refusal again.
- The heights are measured along the tilted tool axis, not along machine Z, so "Z" is not correct for a tilted plane.

## Related

- #2991 fixes the same defect for `FirstTraverseLow` (PR #3080). That PR adds `in_user_frame` in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` and a `tilted` text that names the raise without a Z value.
- Found when main was merged into PR #3080. Main added `FirstTraverseUnderTable` after the review of that PR.

## Possible fix

After #3080 merges: extend `in_user_frame` to `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (add `origin.z` to `height_mm` and `limit_mm`). Change the text so that it does not call a height along the tilted axis a Z value, as #2991 does for `FirstTraverseLow`. A cache field can need `#[serde(default)]`, as `tilted` has in #3080.

## Done means

- The under-table refusal on a 3+2 plane gives the plane and the limit in the frame where the user sets the clearance height.
- The text does not call a height along a tilted tool axis a Z value.
- A test pins the two numbers in the user frame (for the case above: 170 and 133.590), and the post stays blocked.

Proposed labels (a contributor cannot set labels): `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:multiaxis`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`. These are the labels of #2991. The defect is a misleading refusal message with a workaround, so `P3`.

Give `DrillUndersize` a free key (for example `223`). Add a pin in `warning_fold_tests` that folds one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` shank hit and asserts two lines.

The clear-out refresh of PR #2836 found the defect. That refresh moved `UndercutLift` from `217` to `222` for the same reason. This issue is for the `DrillUndersize` key on `main` only.

title: CL toolpath transforms: translate, rotate in XY, rotate about an axis, and mirror across a plane

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Goal

Add a pure toolpath transform module in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` (re-exported by `camcraft-app`). Toolpath patterns, mirror folders, and nesting (`#2166`) share this module.

## Scope

- **Translation (`translate`):** Shift every move, arc center, `Cycle`, `CompSpan`, `EdgeBreak`, and `PlasmaCut` by `(dx, dy, dz)`. Keep coordinates finite and snapped consistently with `crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs` (`lattice`).
- **2D XY rigid transform (`transform_xy`):** Rotate and translate a `Toolpath` in XY by `(tx, ty, angle_deg)` around a pivot. Rotate XY arc centers, cycles, compensation spans, and edge breaks. Flatten or refuse `XZ`/`YZ` vertical arcs clearly. Nesting (`#2166`) calls this function directly.
- **3D rotary axis rotation (`rotate_about_axis`):** Rotate a `Toolpath` about an `A` (X) or `B` (Y) axis through an origin by `angle_deg`. Update `Move::axis` using `crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs` (`TiltedFrame`) and `crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`. Flatten tilted arcs at `chord_tol`.
- **Vertical-plane mirror (`mirror_plane`):** Reflect a `Toolpath` across a vertical plane (`nz == 0`).
  - Refuse horizontal or tilted mirror planes by name (matching `crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`).
  - Under `GeometricMirror`, reflect all coordinates and arc centers, invert `arc.ccw` (`G2` <-> `G3`), and swap `CompSide` (`G41` <-> `G42`), matching `crates/post/src/post/invert.rs` (RS-274 / ISO 6983).
  - Under `PreserveClimb`, reverse planar cutting pass chains safely after entry and before retract (swapping lead-in and lead-out, keeping original `arc.ccw` and `CompSide`) for 2D contours, profiles, and chamfers. Refuse by name any path whose entry or engagement cannot reverse safely (helical ramps, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing).
- **Refusals:** Return a named `TransformError` for unsupported records (turning `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, tilted moves under mirror, non-finite inputs). Add no new crate dependencies.

## Done means

Unit tests in `crates/cl/` verify micron-accurate translation, XY rotation, A/B axis rotation, vertical-plane mirroring (`G2`/`G3` and `G41`/`G42` swap), safe 2D contour pass reversal under `PreserveClimb`, and named refusals for unsupported records and horizontal mirror planes.

Part of #2938

body:
The Wire Contour operation supports open runs with a stated kerf side (#1109). The native Agie post in #2951 accepts only a closed punch.

Post a straight open cut with an explicit left or right side and a supported resident process. Require both wire endpoints to clear opposite faces of the stock. Check the wire, machine travel and hold of the released piece.

A synthetic offline controller job showed why the second start point matters. With both native start points at the entry, the wire made an extra cutting move across the stock after each pass. With a separate exit outside the opposite stock face, all four passes followed their intended offsets. The rough pass releases the piece before the trims start.

Verify the normal CAMCraft operation on both sides. Check the return moves and their compensation against the controller plot. Refuse a missing exit, unsupported holding or an unsafe path before creating the job directory.

Suggested labels are P6, effort:high, area:post, enhancement and source:agent.

Post more than one independently supported cut in a single native Agie job. Today each contour requires a separate job directory.

## Work

Assign a distinct geometry resource, work and threading point to each contour. Check the shared work coordinate system, stock and technology. Check every lead and compensated path against all retained geometry. Refuse touching contours, dependencies on cut order, unsupported setups and any unaccounted workpiece. body:
The maintainer said on 2026-11-20, in the discussion of #2949 (folders as the only source of the machine and post lists):

> Well in this case we need to be able to load mch and cps files from users disk

Now (main at 13f26da99):
- In the browser build the button "Load machine (.mch)" is greyed with the reason "needs a file picker" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_files.rs`, test `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`).
- The file drop (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`) takes only model files: `stl`, `obj`, `step`, `stp` and `sc`.
- A post file (`.cps`) has no browser path at all.
- The browser build has no disk. Once #2949 removes the compiled-in copy, the browser needs another way to get a user's own machine or post file.

Wanted:
- The browser build loads a `.mch` file and a `.cps` file that the user picks or drops. It uses the existing commands (`LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile`), so it is undoable and the MCP tool is the same. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.
- A folder picker (`<input webkitdirectory>`) loads all `.mch` and `.cps` files of one folder, read-only, in one step. It works in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. The File System Access API is not needed.
- The file drop accepts `.mch` and `.cps` files, and several files at once, with each file refused by name and reason if it does not parse. A bad file does not change the project.
- A loaded file shows in the machine list and the post list as a user entry for the session. A saved project that names it by file name gives a refusal by name when the file is not loaded (#2319), not a silent fallback.
- The browser can keep the files for the next session (IndexedDB) if the maintainer wants it. This is a separate decision: put the options in the decision file.

Done means: in the browser build, a picked or dropped `.mch` and `.cps` file is in the lists and a document posts with it. A malformed file is refused by name. A structural test (AccessKit label, role, enabled state) pins each button. The button "Load machine (.mch)" is no longer greyed in the browser.

Related: #2949 (folders only), #2282 (closed), #2414 (merged), #1437 (browser downloads).

body:
## What are you trying to do

Post a rectangular wire EDM punch to an Agie Classic Cut 2S from the desktop or a command script. The controller needs a linked ISO contour, SBR resource list and SBL job. The generic ISO wire post writes a single program.

## How you imagine it working

Select the native post and a compatible machine. Select the controller separation length explicitly. Write all three files to a new job directory. Refuse an unsupported setup without creating output. The controller applies its resident wire compensation to the nominal contour.

The proposed first case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock, with a 0.25 mm wire and a 1 mm separation cut. An offline control accepted a synthetic 40 by 20 mm example. Its graphical check showed a rough pass, three trims and a final separation sequence. This was a software check. A physical machine was not tested.

## Source decision

The proposed writer draws on an independently developed MIT-licensed implementation. Its source notes attribute some interface details to observations of controller examples. The native job uses a resident technology selection. We have not verified a public programming manual for all required call arguments and selection values. No vendor runtime, control image or technology table is proposed for distribution.

Does this reference meet the project's clean-room source rules for an EDM post? If a different reference is required, which published programming reference should we use?

Done means: The project accepts the sources for the post. The desktop and command script produce the same complete native job. Tests pin the supported output, refuse unsupported setups, and preserve an existing destination.

title: 2D Chamfer without picked edges: a plate with one drafted side is refused as a partly bevelled loop

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the read-only second review of PR #2894 (merged). The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it yet.

## What happens

PR #2894 refuses a chamfer with no picked edges when the edge loop is partly bevelled. The check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs` reads each part of the loop whose plan offset from the wall is more than 0.05 mm as "bevelled".

A side with draft also has a plan offset. With a chamfer width of 1 mm and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is above 0.05 mm. Before PR #2894, the chamfer followed that wall, and the result was a valid chamfer. Now the operation is refused, and the message says "modelled chamfer", which is not correct for a drafted side.

## Workaround

Pick the edges.

## What is expected

- A loop that has a drafted side and no modelled chamfer cuts as before, or
- the refusal stays, with a message that names the drafted side correctly, and the decision file of #2887 says so.

The work decides between the two and records the decision.

## Done when

- A test with a plate that has one side drafted more than 3 degrees pins the result.
- The partly bevelled plate of #2887 is still refused.

Refs #2887

title: Slot wider than the tool leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends, and verify is ok

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What

A Slot with a width larger than the tool diameter leaves material in its two round ends. `verify` reports no problem, and the post is not blocked.

The work on the example case `2d/slots` (#2861, part of #2392) found this.

## How to reproduce

On `main` at `ab9955105`, run this script with a model `slots` (a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block, stock of the same size):

```js
cam.call("add_tool", { catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", holder: "none" });
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "Slot", name: "Slot1", tool: "EM-0600-4FL", source: "slots",
  params: {
    a: [-25.0, 15.0], b: [25.0, 15.0], width: 10.0, stock_to_leave: 0.0,
    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
    stepdown: 3.0, stepover: 2.0, feed: 600.0, plunge_feed: 150.0, climb: true
  }
});
cam.generate();
cam.verify();   // ok
```

## What the program does

The tool is 6 mm and the slot is 10 mm wide. The tool centre must stay in a stadium of 2 mm radius around the line `a -> b`. Each level posts three rows:

```
G01 X-25. Y13. Z9. F150
G01 X25. Y13. Z9. F600
G01 X27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-25. Y17. Z9. F600
G01 X25. Y17. Z9. F600
```

The rows touch the round end only at their end points. The tool does not follow the arc between two row ends. The move between two rows is a straight line (a chord), not an arc.

## Measured

A point check of the 10 mm stadium against the tool centre path gives these results:

- The largest leftover is 0.86 mm, on the wall of each round end at 45 degrees, where no move joins two rows.
- The leftover is 0.59 mm at the two corners where a chord joins two rows.
- The total area that is not cut is about 8.9 mm2 for each level.

The straight walls are correct. The rows at `Y13` and `Y17` cut them to size.

## Expected

One of these:

- The Slot cuts its full outline. For example, the tool follows the two half circles of the tool centre stadium at each level.
- The operation reports the leftover as a warning that names the Slot and the largest leftover.

## Workaround

- Use a smaller `stepover`. The leftover becomes smaller, but it does not go to zero.
- Use a Trochoidal slot of the same width. Its last move is a half circle around `b`, and its entry is a full circle around `a`.

## Notes

- The row law is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs` (`SlotParams`: "each row reaches the round ends exactly as far as it can").
- The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` shows the two programs side by side. A fix changes `slots.nc` of that case. Run `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots` with the fix.

Circular must generate safe links between its radial passes, or refuse the parameters before generation with a named cause.

A 5 mm radius with the same tool and plunge entry generates without warnings. The catalog uses this size.

title: Post: Siemens Sinumerik 810M (3-axis mill, older Sinumerik dialect) for the EMCO VMC-200

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Request: a CamCraft user ("Chang Frick" on the SolidCraft Discord #camcraft channel) runs EMCO machines in his garage: an EMCO VMC-200 mill and an EMCO Turn 342 lathe with Siemens Sinumerik controls, plus two VMC-200s being converted to LinuxCNC. His mill control is a **Sinumerik 810M**, an older system. Our only Siemens post, `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps`, targets the **840D**, whose dialect is newer (for example cycle calls, frames and the program header differ).

He offered to help test. He suggested ISO 6983-1 as the starting point.

Clean-room note: he made his own post for Fusion 360. Do not ask for it, read it or use it, and do not read G-code that Fusion produced (AGENTS.md "Clean-Room Protocol": no post processors or output from that product line). Write the post only from public sources: ISO 6983-1, Siemens' published Sinumerik 810M/820M programming documentation (behaviour only), and machine-tool handbooks.

What to find out (in this issue, before code):
- What differs between the 810M and the 840D for 3-axis milling: program start and end, `%` and program numbers, tool change (T/D/M6), offsets (G54-G57, G158/G159 frames), canned cycles (the 810M uses `L` subroutine cycles such as L81..L89 with R parameters, not CYCLE81), arcs (I/J/K vs radius), dwell, coolant and spindle M-codes, comments, block numbers, line length and memory limits.
- Whether the EMCO VMC-200 needs anything machine-specific (tool changer, travel limits, max spindle speed).

Done means: an `assets/posts/sinumerik-810m.cps` post and a machine file for the EMCO VMC-200, with recorded golden outputs for the standard post suites (cycles, arcs, tool change, comp), a provenance line naming the public sources, and a short air-cut kit the owner can run, read back by the user.

body:
Part of #1446. The 2D Adaptive operation takes the `rest` parameter through `edit_operation` (branch `issue/1446-rest-adaptive-op`). The skill file `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` has no row for it. The worker session could not write that file.

PR #2822 (#2033) owes the same file a row for the `source` key of the 2D Pocket. One edit can add the two rows.

Wanted: add this row after the row "2D Pocket rest machining (#1489)".

```
- **2D Adaptive rest machining (#1446)**: `edit_operation { "name": "<2D Adaptive>", "params": { "rest": { "source": "previous_operations", "allowance"?: 0 } } }` makes the 2D Adaptive cut only what the earlier operations of the same setup left. The stock that they leave is read at every cut depth, and each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. `"rest": null` turns it off (off is the default). One undo step; kept in the project file. Generate the earlier operations first. Refused by name at the edit: `source` absent or `entered_tool` (an entered tool proves nothing here; use a 2D Pocket for that mode), a negative or non-finite `allowance`, the Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. Refused by name at `generate`: an earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath or a suppressed cut; no cut ahead to enter from; a roughing pass that stops above the floor of this operation (no entry with proved clearance); "no rest material".
```

Done means: the row is in the skill file, and the PR body has the line `Process change: yes`.

body:
The request of the maintainer (relayed 2026-11-17, quoted in #2392): "have it setup a bunch of examples.. for debugging..". The body of #2392 specifies: "verify clean (no gouge, no refusal unless the case is about a refusal)".

## What

Let a catalog case expect a refusal. `case.toml` gets `expect = "post"` (default) or `expect = "refusal"`. A refusal case has no `.nc` file. It has a file `refusal.txt` with the exact refusal lines.

- The script does not catch the refusal. The script run ends with an error.
- The script saves the project before the refused step.
- The two tests in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` compare the recorded refusal lines with `refusal.txt`, byte for byte.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check` accepts a refusal case that has no `.nc` file.

If the `case.toml` sub-issue of #2392 is not merged, this issue adds the `expect` key itself.

## Evidence

- `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte` asserts `OpStatus::Ok`, an empty verification report and a successful post.
- `every_catalog_case_rebuilds_from_camscript` asserts exit 0 and a written `.nc` file.
- The script host records each refusal in the `errors` list of the run, also when the script catches it (`crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`). This law does not change.

This work is under the safety floor: it changes how a test reads a blocked post.

Done means: one refusal case passes. A changed refusal text makes the test red. A refusal case that posts makes the test red. The script host law does not change.

Part of #2392

title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

body:
Requested by @vilts (relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), after the #2603 kit ran clean in his Robodrill's Manual Guide i graphic simulation: today the simulation draws a default blank, and he does not know how to set it by hand.

## What

Manual Guide i reads a blank (stock) definition block near the top of a program and uses it in the animation. An **opt-in** Fanuc post option writes the setup's stock as that block, after the program number and before the first motion.

Codes as the user's reading of the manual summarises them (to be verified against the manual):

| Code | Blank |
|---|---|
| G1902 | rectangular block: B width (X), D depth (Y), H height (Z), I/J/K = X/Y/Z distance from the block's lowest corner to the work origin |
| G1900 | round bar (along Z) |
| G1906 | round bar along X |
| G1901 / G1907 | hollow round bar (along Z / X) |
| G1903 / G1904 | square bar / hollow square bar |

Example (100 x 60 x 30 block, G54 at the top centre): `G1902 B100. D60. H30. I50. J30. K30.`

Source (public Fanuc documentation, behaviour only): Manual Guide i milling and turning operator's manual, https://www.cnc.uk.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Manual-Guide-Milling-and-Turning-Manual.pdf

## Rules

- **Off by default.** A control without Manual Guide i can alarm on G1902, so the option is per machine (a machine/post property, e.g. "Manual Guide i blank"), never on for every Fanuc output.
- Box stock -> G1902; a cylinder stock -> G1900 (or G1906 when its axis is X); any other stock shape -> no block and a comment saying why, not a wrong block.
- I/J/K come from the setup's WCS origin relative to the stock's minimum corner, in program units (G20/G21), with the signs the manual gives. A yawed or rotated WCS that the block cannot describe -> no block plus a comment.
- No other post output changes (golden files stay the same with the option off).

## Research first (agent)

Read the manual's blank-figure section and confirm: the exact address letters and signs for G1902 and G1900 (incl. the bar's length and the axis position), where in the program the block must stand (before or after G90/G54, before the first tool change), whether it needs Manual Guide i "animation" mode only, and inch behaviour. Record the answers here before code.

## Done means

- The Fanuc post has the option, off by default; with it on, a box stock and a cylinder stock each post the right block (golden tests), and an unsupported stock posts a comment, not a block.
- vilts confirms in his Manual Guide i simulation that the drawn blank matches the stock (one short kit file).
- Clean-room: Fanuc's public manual only; no other CAM's post or output consulted.

title: Research: dynamic test impact analysis for post-merge gates - coverage map + failure history to run likely failures first

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**Research only** (AGENTS.md "needs-research"): answer the questions, then file concrete sub-issues.

## Why
A post-merge gate should **fail fast**: the tests most likely to break after a merge should run first, so a red main is known in minutes, not after ~54 min. Today the order is fixed, and the only change-aware selection is the quick tier's hand-written gate maps (`Gate map (M4.4): covers ...`).

Motivating case (2026-11-19): PR #2664 changed the STEP importer and turned two suites red that its gate maps did not name: `camcraft-app feature_edge_g1_join` and `camcraft-kernel step_agreement` (#2713). Both were found only by the full post-merge run.

## Idea (dynamic, from the code and history - not hand maps)
1. **Coverage map:** after each green full run (or nightly), run the suites under coverage (`cargo llvm-cov`, per test) and store a map: test -> files/functions it executed. On a merge, the tests that executed the changed lines run first. (Here: `step_agreement` executes the STEP importer, so it would have ranked first.)
2. **Failure history:** record, per gate run, which tests failed and which files changed. Rank tests by P(fail | changed files) / duration; boost recent failures and new tests.
3. **Graph fallback:** the repo's graphify graph (`graphify affected`) for test -> code wiring when no coverage data exists for a file.
4. **Execution:** feed the ranked list to a parallel runner (nextest or the release-queue lanes, #2727), which starts each test as soon as its binary is built. The FULL suite still runs; ranking only changes the ORDER (the map can be wrong; a skip must never hide a failure).

## Open questions
1. Cost and stability of a per-test coverage run for the whole workspace (time on a 16-32 vCPU box; size of the map; how often to refresh it).
2. Granularity: file, function or line; how renames and moved code keep their history.
3. How the ranking reaches the gate (an input file to `xtask`, or a nextest filter/order).
4. Where the history lives (a file in the repo, a gate artifact, the post-merge workflow's cache).
5. Measured value: replay recent red post-merge runs and report time-to-first-failure with and without ranking.

## Measurements so far (#2727)
Same green commit 3a240b7fb: post-merge gate 53.4 min (warm, steps one at a time; 731 of 898 steps <= 1 s); `cargo nextest run` over the same scope 18.8 min cold on 16 vCPU, 8465 tests passed.

Done means: the questions are answered in comments, the sub-issues are filed (each with a P*, effort, area, Done-means, "Part of #this"), and this umbrella is closed.

Related: #2727, #2556, #2557, #2713.

body:
Add a clean-room 2-axis wire EDM post (`assets/posts/g-edm.cps`) for G-EDM / `G-RBLv3` controllers.

## Context

`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` requires `edm.codes.condition` (with `{id}`) and `edm.codes.comp_off`, and it writes `%` tape fences. Public G-EDM documentation (`gedm.org`, `github.com/G-EDM/G-RBL`) states that DIY G-EDM builds control spark power at the controller or firmware instead of via G-code condition words, and `Grbl_Esp32` / Grbl v1.1 rejects bare `%` fences (`error:20`) and `G41`/`G42` radius compensation.

## What this does

- Add `assets/posts/g-edm.cps` (`vendor = "Camcraft"`, `wireEdm = true`, `afterModes = true`, `programUnits = "mm inch"`), with provenance citing public `gedm.org` and `Grbl_Esp32` documentation. Read no `G-RBLv3` source code.
- Register `"G-EDM Wire EDM"` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS`) and `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS` and `embedded()`). Keep `"Generic ISO Wire EDM"` as the default (`WIRE_POSTS[0]`).
- Write `(NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)` and condition reminders as `(...)` header comments. Do not require `edm.codes`.
- Emit `G21`/`G20`, `G90`, `G17`, `G0`, `G1`, `G2`/`G3` (`I`/`J`), and `M30`, with no `%` fence, no `O`-word, and no `G41`/`G42`.
- Refuse non-`wire_edm` machines, rotaries, `Z` changes, `WireTaper != 0`, `WireFourAxis`, `WireU`/`WireV`, `WireAngle`, `onRadiusCompensation`, `skims`, `onCycle`, `onToolChange`, `SpindleSpeed > 0`, and `AfterOperation === "home"` by name.
- Check `#2697` before coding for any new `G-RBLv3` answers from the reporter (for example whether `G1` requires a dummy `F` word to avoid Grbl `error:22`, `G40`, `M00` threading pauses, or a return move to origin).
- Add golden and refusal tests (`crates/app/tests/g_edm_post.rs`, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/`, `crates/post/tests/script_g_edm.rs`, `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`), and update `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS`).

## Done means:

- `"G-EDM Wire EDM"` posts a 2-axis `WireContour` golden without `edm.codes` through `posting::post_script`.
- Non-`wire_edm` machines, `G41`/`G42`, taper, 4-axis, skims, and mill goldens refuse by name.
- `cargo xtask gate test g_edm --crate camcraft-app`, `cargo xtask gate test conformance --crate camcraft-app`, and `cargo xtask gate test script_g_edm --crate camcraft-post` pass.

Part of #2697

title: Research: G-EDM (DIY EDM, Grbl-based G-RBLv3 firmware) - wire EDM post and machine file

labels.name: enhancement

body:
**Research only.** No code until the open questions are answered and the concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Where this comes from

Alex (@alextreseder; CamCraft Discord, 2026-11-19), who already helps with XYUV wire paths in #2690, is building a DIY EDM with the **G-EDM** spark generator and motion control. We may need a CamCraft post and machine file for it.

## What is public about G-EDM (from its project pages)

- Firmware **G-RBLv3** (github.com/G-EDM/G-RBLv3): a fork of Grbl (via Grbl_Esp32) reduced to a module inside the G-EDM code, for wire and sinker EDM machines on the G-EDM EVO / Gapstorm electronics.
- **Wire EDM runs from G-code files.** **Sinker EDM does not:** the firmware makes the sinker motion itself.
- The developer explains why stock Grbl/Marlin/LinuxCNC fit EDM poorly: the gap must be servo-controlled, and a feed hold can overrun the short-to-spark gap.
- **Licence:** the repository says its files are for private use only unless declared otherwise; commercial use and redistribution are prohibited. It is source-available, not open source.

## Clean-room and licence limits

- We use the **public behaviour and documentation** only (which G-code words the firmware reads, units, arcs, the meaning of feed), and the owner's own observations. We **do not copy or derive code** from G-RBLv3 (its licence forbids it, and the clean-room rule applies to everything we ship).
- No material from Autodesk products.

## Open questions

1. Which G-code subset does G-RBLv3 accept for wire EDM: units, absolute/incremental, G2/G3 arcs (I/J or R), G41/G42 or pre-offset paths only, comments, program start/end?
2. Is it 2-axis (XY) only, or does it support U/V (taper / XYUV, which ties to #2690)?
3. What does F mean on an EDM gap-servo machine: a maximum feed, or ignored? Which M-codes switch the spark, flushing, wire feed and tension, if any?
4. Can CamCraft's existing wire path (Wire Contour, kerf offset, skims) map onto it, or is a different structure needed (e.g. one pass, the firmware sets the conditions)?
5. Is sinker EDM in scope at all, given that the firmware makes the sinker motion itself (maybe only a setup/position export)?
6. What machine-file data do we need (travels, wire diameter, guide heights)?

## What would help (from Alex)

- Which G-EDM electronics and firmware version he runs, and whether his build is wire, sinker or both.
- A short wire program that his G-EDM accepts (any simple shape), and anything the firmware refuses.
- Later: a dry run of a CamCraft test program, no cutting needed.

Related: #2690 (XYUV swallowtails), #617 (Sodick wire post), the existing `wire-iso` post.

## Done means

The questions above are answered in comments, and the concrete sub-issues (post, machine file, refusals) are filed, each with one P*, one effort label, area labels, a Done-means line and "Part of #this"; then this umbrella is closed.

title: Viewport: draw an arrow and the text "Operator side" at the work envelope

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue, p4, in the work envelope. there should be a Arrow "pointing" towards the user and the text stating "operator side".. so people understand where they look "into" the work envelope from.

## Problem

The viewport shows the work envelope of the machine. A user cannot tell from which side the operator looks into it. The user then does not know how the part sits, how the vise faces, or which way is "front".

## Wanted

1. The work envelope shows an arrow on the operator side. The arrow points toward the operator, away from the envelope. The text "Operator side" is next to the arrow.
2. The side comes from the machine. A 3-axis mill and a 4-axis or 5-axis machine have a default operator side (the front of the machine). A lathe, a router table, a laser or a plasma table can differ. The machine file may name the side. When it does not, a documented default for the machine type applies. A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records the defaults.
3. The arrow and the text follow the view: the text stays readable, the arrow stays at the envelope edge in 3D, and both do not hide the part or the toolpath. Draw them with the envelope, in the envelope colour or a muted one.
4. A switch hides them. Default: shown. The switch is a view setting (ephemeral UI state, no undo command). It sits with the other envelope display options.
5. The label text is plain English and is the same in all views. No G-code words.

## Constraints

- Layers: ui reads the machine data through the app API. A new machine-file field follows the machine-file rules and keeps old files valid (the field is optional).
- No per-frame work that can be cached (frame target under 10 ms). Build the arrow geometry once for each envelope change.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert the presence, the text, the side for each machine type and the switch state, not pixel values. Update the layout test of the viewport page if it applies.
- Draw an original arrow. Use no asset from another product.

## Done means

- A test shows the arrow and the text for a mill, with the side as the default says.
- A test shows a machine file that names another side, and that an old file without the field still loads.
- A test shows that the switch hides and shows them.
- The PR has before and after screenshots.

body:

The order of the maintainer (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What
Add the GPU material removal kernel to `camcraft-gpu` (the crate of #2620).

- Parity on the software adapter (`headless_gpu` policy of #2620) against the S1 CPU twin:
  - bit equal on the same adapter in two runs;

- With no adapter: a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` makes it a failure (#615).
- Measure the time for one batch on the software adapter, and write it in the PR.

A `docs/decisions/` entry for the `camcraft-gpu -> camcraft-sim` edge is necessary (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision"). It lists the imported items: the sweep and tool data, the lattice meta, `CutPatch`, the pack functions.

title: GPU compute seam: a headless compute crate with capability probe, CPU fallback and one parity-tested kernel (facet binning)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 2 of 5. Needs slice 1 (#2619) for the CPU reference.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
Only `camcraft-ui` links wgpu today, through the `egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export (`Cargo.toml` lines 46-47). The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They have no GPU access. The headless device policy exists, but in `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`.

## What
- A new crate (recommended name `camcraft-gpu`) for headless compute. It holds:
  - The device policy of `headless_gpu.rs` (software adapter first in tests, then hardware), moved down from `camcraft-ui`. `camcraft-ui` then uses it.
  - A capability probe: `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroup_storage_size`. WebGL2 and GL below ES 3.1 have no compute: the probe says "no compute" by name.
  - One device for each process, made on the first request and cached (`OnceLock`). Never made for each operation or each frame.
  - A switch to turn the GPU off (recommended: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`) for tests and for machines with bad drivers (#2424, #74).
  - One kernel: conservative facet binning. Input: facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` plus a margin. Output: the cell lists.
- The CPU path runs, with the same result, when there is no adapter, the probe fails, the device is lost, or a buffer is past the limit. The log names the reason one time. Never a panic, never `unwrap` on a GPU future.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- Superset parity: for the same facets, each facet in the CPU grid cell of #2619 is in the GPU cell list. Extra GPU entries are permitted.
- Refusals: a buffer past the limit, and a forced "no compute" probe, give `Err` with the reason. The caller uses the CPU grid.
- Adapter policy: the `headless_gpu` rule (#615). No adapter prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns the skip into a failure. The self-hosted runners have the Mesa software drivers (`runners` skill), so the lane runs on lavapipe there.

## Decision entry and dependencies
- A `docs/decisions/` entry is necessary: new crate edges (`camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` onto the new crate). The entry lists the imported items and what rebuilds.
- A direct `wgpu` dependency is new for the workspace. The version must be the one that the egui set pins (`=30.0.1` with egui-wgpu `=0.36.2`), so no second wgpu enters the lock. The review sets `needs-maintainer` for this dependency, by AGENTS.md.
- The wgpu version then moves with the egui set (#658, #1118). The decision entry says so.
- `camcraft-motion` gets no GPU dependency. The app computes the GPU result and passes it into motion as a value.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, new behaviour with its tests). No posted output changes in this slice.

Done means: the new crate exists with the probe, the cached device, the CPU fallback and the binning kernel; the superset parity test passes on the software adapter; `camcraft-ui` uses the moved device policy; the decision entry is in the PR.

title: Simulation: add a step button that jumps to the start of the next operation

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> when hitting simulation there sh ould be an option to "step" thru to next operation.. so we can check the one relevant

## Problem

The simulation plays the whole program from the first move. A user who wants to check one operation must scrub or wait. There is no way to go to the next operation.

## Wanted

1. The simulation controls have a "next operation" step. It moves the playback position to the first move of the next operation in program order.
2. A matching "previous operation" step. It moves to the start of the current operation, and a second press moves to the start of the one before it.
3. The control shows which operation is current (its name from the tree). A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change works the same as a step inside one setup.
4. The stock shown at the new position is correct: it is the stock after all earlier operations. A step must give the same stock as playback to that position. A step never skips a removal.
5. Disabled states: "next" is disabled in the last operation. "previous" is disabled at the start of the first operation. The AccessKit labels and the tooltips say what each button does.
6. A keyboard shortcut for each step, listed in the shortcut help.

## Notes

- The playback position is ephemeral UI state (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"), so no undoable command is needed. If a step selects an operation in the tree, that selection goes through `SelectEntity`.
- A skipped or suppressed operation is not a stop. An operation with no toolpath is not a stop.
- UI text: plain English, no G-code jargon. A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and the position, not pixel values (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`).
- Related: #2587 (the stand-alone simulator window). The same step logic should work there. Keep the operation-boundary lookup in the lowest crate that provides it, so both can use it.

## Done means

- A test shows that "next" from a position inside operation 1 gives the first move of operation 2, and that the stock equals the stock from plain playback to that move.
- Tests for the first operation, the last operation, a tool change and an operation with no toolpath.
- The behaviour tests and the page layout test of the simulation panel pass.

title: Machine file: reserved tool numbers (the probe's pocket), so a cutting tool is never given that T number

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

title: Post: Mach3 Mill (3-axis), separate from the Mach4 post

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Request

Add a post for Mach3 Mill (3-axis). Mach3 is still on many retrofit mills and routers. The `Mach4` post writes words and macros that Mach3 does not read in the same way.

## Differences to the Mach4 post

From the public "Using Mach3Mill" manual (behaviour only):

- Canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98` / `G99`. `G84` needs a tapping head setup: refuse a tap by name unless the machine file says that tapping is available.
- `G4 P` dwell: Mach3 reads P in seconds or in milliseconds by a setting ("G04 dwell param in ms"). The post must have an option for this. Default: seconds, as in the manual.
- Tool change: `T<n> M6`, then `G43 H<n>`. The `M6` behaviour depends on the user's `M6Start` / `M6End` macros, so the post does not assume a retract inside `M6`. It retracts first.
- Arcs: the IJ mode (absolute or incremental) is a Mach3 setting. The post must not depend on it: it writes the IJ mode word that the user selects in an option (default incremental IJ). The goldens must be checked against the manual for the word that Mach3 reads. A header comment names the mode.
- No Custom Macro B (`#` variables in expressions). The Mach4 post uses `[...]` expressions in some places; the Mach3 post must write plain numbers only.
- Program end `M30`. Comments `( )`.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Mach3` and a machine file.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill, peck, bore, two tools, and the dwell option in both modes.
- A test that no `[` expression and no `#` variable is posted.

I can do this work in a PR from my fork.

**Decision**
- CamCraft gets no Router tab.
- A machine of kind Router shows the Nest node and the router options on the Milling tab. It hides the operations and options that do not apply to a router.

**Why**
- The router functions are jobs at sheet level (nesting, grain, labels, remnants) and options on operations that exist (tabs, corner relief, drill blocks). They are not one operation family.
- Nesting has its own tree node in #2163.

**Scope**
1. The machine file states the kind Router where it does not do so now. The check starts with the router machines of #1915 and #1918.
2. One function decides which operations, pages and options a machine kind shows. The UI and MCP read the same function.
3. A hidden operation that is already in a project stays visible and is not deleted.
4. The router sub-issues attach their options to this function: #2398, #2399, #2400, #2401, #2402, #2404, #2405, #2406, #2407, #2408, #2409.

Done means:
- A project with a router machine shows the router options on the Milling tab.
- A project with a mill shows no router option.

title: Nesting: add global sheet cut-order tree and parts-in-holes safety in camcraft-geometry

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Add a global sheet cut-order tree, hold-down sequencing, and cut-side planner in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/` (reusing the nesting rules from `crates/motion/src/plasma/nest.rs`).

Depends on #2158 and #1861.

## Scope

- Build one global containment forest across all closed contours and open chains on a nested sheet.
- Assign each open chain to its smallest enclosing closed contour, or mark it top-level when outside all parts.
- Assign each contour and chain a resolved cut role and cut side:
  - Closed loops: `Outside`, `OnLine`, or `Inside` (`Auto` sets outer part outlines to `Outside`, holes to `Inside`, and islands inside holes to `Outside`).
  - Open chains: `OnLine`, `Left`, or `Right`.
  - Refuse `Inside` or `Outside` on an open chain by name.
- Traverse the global containment tree in deterministic iterative post-order:
  - Cut internal holes, pockets, and open features of a part before its outer outline.
  - Cut small parts nested inside a hole before the enclosing hole cuts free.
  - Order sibling parts at the same depth by increasing area (small parts before large parts) to preserve router vacuum hold-down and sheet rigidity.
  - Reserve ordered pass phases: marking/scribe passes (`#1447`) first, internal/pocket passes next, rough/onion-skin profile passes next, and final onion-skin breakthrough passes last.
- Compute minimum inside-corner cutter-radius clearance diagnostics when a circular tool (`radius = cut_width / 2`) cannot reach sharp concave corners.
- Validate that no contour cuts after an enclosing contour has already freed its material.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/geometry` verify inside-out cut order across a multi-part sheet containing nested holes, internal open cuts, and a small part placed inside a large hole, verify phase ordering for marking and onion-skin passes, confirm smaller sibling parts precede larger ones deterministically, report concave inside-corner radius limits, and refuse invalid open-chain side requests by name.

Part of #2156

title: 2D rest machining: derive remaining material from previous operations

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Part of #1490.

The rest generator currently trusts an entered previous tool. It assumes that tool cut the pocket to the requested depth.

Add a previous-operations mode that derives remaining material from the stock those operations actually leave.

Design decision:
- Keep the entered-tool mode explicit. Add a separate previous-operations mode through an undoable command, the project file, and MCP.
- Read only earlier operations in the same setup, in their actual order. Reuse the established carried-stock infrastructure.
- Require current operation paths and compatible setup coordinates. Refuse missing, stale, or unsupported stock by name, or mark the result incomplete.
- Read remaining stock at every requested cut depth. A shallow roughing pass does not prove that the lower floor is clear.
- Include tool shape, wall and floor allowances, and the supported simulation resolution. Unknown cells remain occupied.
- Pass a conservative remaining-material region to the motion generator. Do not infer cleared volume from the previous tool diameter alone.
- Invalidate the result when an earlier operation changes, moves, is suppressed, or changes its tool or depth.
- Keep the current stock backend. Do not combine this feature with the field-engine migration in #586 or #637.

Tests:
- Compare the rest region with independently simulated earlier operations.
- Test mixed previous tool sizes, bull-nose tools, partial depths, wall allowances, islands, and disconnected cuts.
- Test missing paths, stale paths, operation reordering, changed tools, and unsupported stock frames.
- Prove the plan never removes material from its rest estimate unless the earlier cuts prove that material absent.
- Prove command undo, project save and reopen, MCP editing, and dependency invalidation.
- Remove each depth and stock-validity guard separately. Each mutation must fail its pinning test.

Done means: previous-operations mode uses conservative stock at each depth, passes these tests, and never guesses when stock cannot be established.

Related: #586 and #637 migrate the stock representation. This issue consumes the current representation for 2D rest machining.

Literature: M. Held, On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining, LNCS 500 (1991), https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9. Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta and D. S. Nau, Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems, Computer-Aided Design 35 (2003), https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The per-depth stock and invalidation contract above is this project's decision. Do not copy another CAM product's code or output.

title: Post: add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (richauto.cps) with conformance goldens

labels.name: enhancement
