body:
Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

Part of #1907

Add a separate `OpType::MultiAxisDeburr` operation in `Section::MultiAxis` for 4-axis and 5-axis edge breaks with holder collision avoidance.

Depends on #1891 (3D `EdgeBreak` verification).

## Where

- `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs` (`OpType`), `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `sane.rs`, `area.rs`
- `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` (`KindInfo::ALL`), `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`

1. Add `OpType::MultiAxisDeburr` and append it at the end of `KindInfo::ALL` (after ordinal `43` `SinkerSideBurn`) in `Section::MultiAxis` so saved operation ordinals never shift.

- Both 4-axis and 5-axis modes tilt cleanly around holder obstacles within `max_tilt_deg`, emit multi-axis CL moves that verify and post clean, and work end-to-end in UI and MCP.

body:
Standardize 3D `Deburr` on chamfer chord width `w`, add Constant Depth sizing, and support multi-pass edge breaks.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs` (`DeburrParams`)
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs` (`deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte`)
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `sane.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`
- `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` (`PROJECT_VERSION`), `crates/app/src/mcp/`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`

## What to change

1. Redefine `DeburrParams.width` and `OpParams::Deburr.width` as chamfer chord width `w = 2 * s * sin(theta / 2)` across all wedge angles `theta` (default `0.5 mm`). Keep `Chamfer2D.width` unchanged as its 2D horizontal leg width.
2. Increment `PROJECT_VERSION` (`61` -> `62`) and multiply legacy 3D `Deburr.width` values by `sqrt(2)` on load (the 90-degree corner ratio). Update `deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte` to pass `w = 2.0 * sqrt(2)`.
3. Add `break_mode` (`ConstantWidth` default, `ConstantDepth`), `break_profile` (`Chamfer` default, `Round`), and multi-pass step parameters to `DeburrParams` and `OpParams::Deburr`.
4. Compute setback `s = d / cos(theta / 2)` for `ConstantDepth`. Emit outer-to-final cone chamfer passes within `EdgeBreak::floor_at`, and refuse `Round` by name on sharp cones until ball-tipped cutters run.
5. Wire all settings through commands, project files, MCP `ParamsDto`, and UI controls.

## Done means

- Legacy v61 `Deburr` projects migrate cleanly by `sqrt(2)` and keep matching cut depth on 90-degree corners.
- `ConstantWidth` and `ConstantDepth` cones cut multi-pass bevels that stay inside `EdgeBreak` bounds and pass verify.
- `Round` on a sharp cone refuses by name, and UI, MCP, and migration tests pass.

Part of #1827

body:
Add a dedicated `WaterjetProfile` 2D through-cut operation by extracting shared sheet-cutting helpers from `motion::plasma` and `motion::wire_edm`.

Depends on #1881 and #1882.

## Scope

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/`):**
  - Extract pure contour nesting (`nest.rs`), `Region::offset` kerf rings (`ring.rs`), `kerf_law` / `cover_law` (`laws.rs`), open-contour left/right offsets (`wire_edm/open.rs`), and flat tab splitting (`wire_edm/tabs.rs`) into shared helpers.
  - Reuse those helpers across `plasma`, `wire_edm`, and `waterjet` without duplicating geometry logic.
  - Add straight and arc lead-in/lead-out support on open chains created by tab gaps (`crates/motion/src/plasma/emit.rs` currently cuts open chains on centerline with no leads).
- **Waterjet profile generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`):**
  - Cut inner holes before enclosing outer contours.
  - Offset geometry by half-kerf (outside, inside, or left/right open chains) with optional control compensation (`G41`/`G42`) when supported.
  - Cut flat tabs as uncut gaps (`count`, `width`, `at`) that turn closed loops into open chains with safe pierce leads outside the part edge.
  - Handle tight holes by shortening leads to clear opposite kerf or center-piercing when needed, without plasma THC assumptions.
  - Apply configurable arc linearization (`Move::chords(tol)`) when enabled.
- **App, commands, persistence, and UI (`crates/app`, `crates/ui`):**
  - Register `OpType::WaterjetProfile`, `Family::Waterjet`, and `Section::Waterjet` in `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`.
  - Add undoable commands, `.camproj` serialization DTO, UI ribbon mode/icon/page (kerf side, leads, tabs, pierce and abrasive dwell, cut-data selection, without plasma height/THC fields).

**Done means:** `WaterjetProfile` generates inner-first kerf-offset paths with leads on closed contours and tabbed open chains, round-trips in `.camproj` via undoable commands, shows in the UI on `Kind::Waterjet` machines, and matches golden CL output for a tabbed plate with holes.

Part of #1525

Depends on #1881 (`waterjet` machine kind and `Waterjet` tool kind).

## Scope

- **Post engine (`crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`, `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`, `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs`):**
  - Add an optional `lineEnding` manifest flag (`"lf"` default, `"crlf"` for `\r\n` output) in `js.rs` and `engine.rs` (lines 528–532 write only `\n` today).

Maintainer request and safety requirement from #1572 ("Units: the converted STEP's units are stated in the import summary; a file with no units asks, never guesses.").

## Goal
Report resolved STEP length units on import and stop silent millimeter assumptions when direct or `cadmpeg`-converted STEP files omit unit declarations.

## Scope
- Update `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_units.rs` (`mm_per_unit` or a typed result) so it returns the resolved unit label (`mm`, `in`, `m`, etc.) and scale factor, or an explicit missing-unit state (`None`).
- Remove the silent `.unwrap_or(1.0)` fallback in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs`.
- Extend `Graded`, `ImportModel`, and `UpdateModel` (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs`, `crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`, `crates/app/src/commands/update_model.rs`) with optional explicit `unit_override: Option<Unit>` (`mm` or `in`) and record the resolved unit in `notes`.
- When a direct or `cadmpeg`-converted STEP file omits `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` length units and the caller provides no `unit_override`, return a dedicated missing-units error (`CommandError::Needs` / typed `ImportError`) instead of guessing millimeters.
- Add a desktop UI prompt asking the user to pick `mm` or `in` when `ImportFile` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) hits a unitless STEP file, then replay `ImportModel` with the chosen unit without adding partial undo entries.
- Update any existing unitless STEP test fixtures in `crates/` to declare STEP units or supply explicit units where headless tests call `ImportModel` directly.
- Add unit and UI prompt tests covering explicit STEP units (`mm`, `in`, `m`), missing-unit headless refusal, missing-unit UI prompt completion and cancellation, and `notes` reporting.

## Done means
Direct and converted STEP imports state source length units in `notes`; unitless STEP imports ask `mm` or `in` in the UI and refuse by name in headless calls unless `units` is given, with tests passing.

title: Sinker EDM: the size law refuses a finish of a cavity with sharp corners that are not square to the axes

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Part of #1152 (and #543). Found while working #1152.

**What happens:** the size law (`sinker_undersize::judge`) judges a body electrode on the X and Y extents of its outline. An inward offset moves a sharp corner that is not square to the axes further than the undersize. For such a cavity (a diamond, a rotated rectangle) the extents that the spark gap reaches are short of the cavity's extents. A finish pass is then refused: "sinker finish leaves the cavity under size". A rough pass and a single pass are generated.

The refusal is true to the model: a round gap does not reach a sharp corner. But the user cannot make a finish pass of such a cavity, and the stock sim judges the same burn clean within its tolerance.

**What is wanted:** the size law compares the electrode's outline with the cavity's outline, not their extents. The Sinker Burn then states the cavity's outline (today it states `cavity_x` and `cavity_y` only). A finish is refused only when a wall is left under size by more than the slack.

**Evidence:** `crates/motion/src/sinker_undersize.rs` (the module head and `Undersize::outline`), `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_body.rs` (`a_cavity_turned_from_the_axes_is_judged_on_its_outlines_extents`), `docs/decisions/1152-electrode-body.md`.

**Done means:** a finish pass of a diamond pocket with the electrode that `electrode_from_faces` makes for its finish condition is generated, and the program verdict judges it clean. An electrode that is too large for the cavity is still refused by name. The new parameter has its MCP schema entry.

title: macOS: sign and notarize the release app so Gatekeeper opens it without a workaround

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

Open CamCraft on a Mac after downloading it from the releases page, without having to override Gatekeeper.

The macOS app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized (`scripts/package-macos.sh`: "Distribution signing and notarization can replace this when credentials exist"). A browser download gets the quarantine flag, and macOS then blocks the first launch because Apple can't verify the developer. Every new release is a new copy, so a user has to override Gatekeeper again after each update.

The README says the first launch "may require Control-click → Open". Since macOS 15 (Sequoia) that no longer works for an app that isn't notarized: the user has to try to open it, then go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CamCraft.app` in Terminal.

### How you imagine it working

The release signs the macOS app with a Developer ID certificate and notarizes it, so it opens like any other downloaded app. It would work the same way Windows signing does now (`scripts/sign.ps1`):

- `scripts/package-macos.sh` signs with Developer ID (hardened runtime, secure timestamp) when signing credentials are configured through the environment, and keeps today's ad-hoc signature, with a printed "unsigned" line, when they aren't. Unsigned stays a valid release.
- When credentials are configured, the release job submits the ZIP or DMG with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then staples the ticket to the app and the DMG with `xcrun stapler staple`.
- The certificate and the notary credentials (an App Store Connect API key, or an Apple ID with an app-specific password) live in repository secrets, as the Windows PFX does.

This needs an Apple Developer Program membership, so whether and when to do it is the maintainer's call. A smaller step that helps meanwhile: update the README's macOS line to the macOS 15 steps above.

title: 3D Finish requires a ball nose; flat-tool z-level finishing of fillets is refused

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

The part is a 30 mm cube made of two L-shaped halves with 15 mm quadrant steps. Every edge, convex and concave, has an R3.125 mm fillet. The only cutter is a 1/4 in (6.35 mm) 3-flute **flat** end mill.

- **3D Finish takes only a ball nose** (`list_operation_types`: `"tool_kinds": ["BallNose"]`). With the flat end mill, the op is refused:
  `No ball-nose in Setup 2's tools - a 3D Finish operation cuts with one; add it ... 'BN-0600' (6 mm ball-nose)`
- There is no **z-level (waterline) finish** with a flat or bull-nose tool. That is the usual way to finish steep walls and convex fillets with the tool already in the spindle.
- The workaround was a **3D Pocket** with 0.15 mm (0.006 in) stepdowns used as "terraces" over the top fillets. That is a roughing strategy, so it leaves the 0.15 mm stair-steps the user has to accept. It also hit `feed moves ... cross in XY at shared depth` on the notch path.

## Expected

A finishing strategy that works with flat and bull-nose cutters:

- **z-level / waterline contours** on the model at a set stepdown (or scallop height), at least for steep regions;
- the tool's real shape (flat bottom, corner radius) used for the gouge offset;
- the shallow areas left to a later pass or flagged as rest.

A flat tool still cannot form a concave fillet smaller than its corner radius, and the rest check should say so. It can follow convex fillets and walls.

**Done means:** 3D Finish (or a new 3D Contour kind) accepts flat and bull-nose tools with a z-level pattern. On a filleted block with a flat end mill it generates gouge-free waterline passes at the set stepdown, and verify reports the concave-fillet rest. A pinning test covers the flat and bull-nose cases.

Related: #763 (3D work in an aligned setup, needed for the same part's bottom side).

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: rest machining exists for 3D operations, but a 2D Pocket (and 2D Adaptive) cannot be limited to what a larger previous tool left: a small finishing tool re-cuts the whole pocket in air.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive, a "Rest machining" group: on/off, source (previous tool diameter and corner radius entered by hand, or "from the previous operations" using the carried stock), and a rest allowance. The path covers only the regions the previous tool could not reach (corners, narrow necks), entered from already cut space where there is any.

Safety: the rest region must be a superset of the material really left. Under-reading it leaves a full-width cut for a small tool, which breaks it. With the hand-entered source the op says in its summary that it trusts the entered tool; with the carried-stock source the regions are checked against the stock simulation in a test.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on 2D rest-region computation (offset differences, medial-axis reach of a tool); the code is written from that and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: a pocket with 3 mm corners roughed by a 12 mm tool gets a rest pass with a 4 mm tool that cuts only the corners (golden CL); simulation shows no passes over cleared floor and no plunge into uncut stock; undo/redo; MCP parameters; a previous tool smaller than the current one is refused by name; the literature used is cited in the PR.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." What is missing: there is no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth; it does not set depth from the width of the region.

For closed regions (text, signs, inlays) the tool centre follows the medial axis and the depth at each point is the one where the cone touches both walls, limited by a maximum depth. Where the region is wider than the cone reaches at maximum depth, an optional flat-clearing pass (same or a second flat tool) removes the floor. Parameters are user choices with defaults: max depth, flat clearing on/off and its tool, start depth, stepdown for deep carves.

Safety: the cone must never cut outside the selected region at any depth (pinned by a test that sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline). A tool that is not a V-bit, an open region, or a tip flat larger than the narrowest feature is refused by name. Undoable command, MCP tool, simulation and collision checks like any 2D op.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published papers and handbooks on medial-axis / Voronoi-based V-carving; the algorithm is written from those and named in the module provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: a V-carve op on a closed text outline generates, simulates without leaving the region, posts through the existing posts, has a golden CL file and an MCP tool; fuzzed degenerate regions (self-intersecting, zero-width) give a clean error; the literature used is cited in the PR and the provenance comment.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
